full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub, J: This Rule Nisi was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the deprivation of the petitioner of promotion to the post of Joint Director in Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy (RDA), Garidaho, Sherpur, Bogura despite having fulfilled all criterions for promotion to the said post and at the same time giving promotion to the respondent Nos.5-9 to the post of Joint Director upon superseding the petitioner vide Memo No.47.00.0000.033.12. 027.19.223 dated 5-8-2019 issued by the respondent No.1 and the office order dated 6-8-2019 issued by the respondent No.2 under Memo No.47.64.1088.014.12.030.15/845 (Annexure D) despite the fact that the respondent Nos. 5-9 were junior to the petitioner and that the initial appointment of respondent No.5 was made at the age of over 42 years, should not be declared to have been done without any lawful authority, and hence, of no legal effect and also, as to why the respondent Nos.1-4 should not be directed to promote the petitioner to the post of Joint Director with retrospective seniority from the date of promotion of his immediate junior officers in the gradation list.
2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the respondent Nos. 1-4 were directed to reserve 1(one) post of Joint Director in Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy subject to disposal of the instant Rule Nisi.
3. Facts, in brief, are that Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy, also known as Rural Development Academy (RDA), Bogura is a statutory body established under the Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy Ain, 1990 (in short, the Ain, 1990). Said Academy is a specialized institution for rural development related training, research etc. It also provides advisory services and offers post graduate diploma.
4. In exercise of power as provided under section 21 of the said Ain, 1990 the Board of Governors of the Academy framed "Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy Karmachari Chakuri Probidhanmala, 1990" (in short, the Regulations, 1990) to provide for the organogram of the Academy and to regulate the terms and conditions of services of its employees including their appointment and promotion respectively. Subsequently, said Regulations was re-pealed and re-formulated as "Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy Karmachari Chakuri Probidhanmala, 2015" (in short, the Regulations, 2015).
5. The petitioner was initially appointed in the post of Assistant Director in Bogura Pally Unnayan Academy. He joined in the said post on 10-11-2004. Subsequently, by virtue of his satisfactory service record he was promoted to the post of Deputy Director vide office order dated 1-4-2012 (Annexure B).
6. In this regard, the contention of the petitioner is that since he had joined in the Academy on 10-11-2004 and since 1-4-2012 he is serving in the current post of Deputy Director as such, he is senior to respondent Nos.5-9 as per the gradation list of Deputy Directors, as prepared and circulated by the Academy on 18-2-2019 (Annexure C).
7. Rural Development and Co-operative Division under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (in short, LGRD) vide Memo No.47.00.0000.033. 12.027.19.223 dated 5-8-2019 recommended 6(six) Deputy Directors for promotion to the post of Joint Director. With reference to the aforesaid Memo dated 5-8-2019, the respondent No.2, the Director-General of the Academy vide the impugned Memo No.47.64.1088.014.12.030. 15/845 dated 6-8-2019(Annexure D) gave promotion to the respondent Nos.5-9 and another to the post of Joint Director. In this regard, the contention of the petitioner is that said impugned promotion has been given to the respondents concerned despite the fact that respondent Nos. 5-9 were junior to him as per the gradation list dated 18-2-2019(Annexure C) and that considering the date of birth of the respondent No.5 his age was over 42 years on the date of his appointment in the post of Deputy Director of the Academy, which is a violation of the Service Regulations, 1990, as it was in force at the relevant time, as well as under the Regulations, 2015 respectively.
8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with, the petitioner has preferred the instant application and obtained the present Rule Nisi.
9. Mr Md Bodruddoza, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Md Reajul Hasan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had joined in the Academy on 10-11-2004 and is serving in the current post of Deputy Director since 1-4-2012; hence, he fulfills the requirement of 10(ten) years service period in the respective post including 5(five) years as Deputy Director for promotion to the post of Joint Director. In this regard, he also submits that the petitioner had successfully completed respective professional courses like, the Cereal System Initiative for South Asia (CSISA) and the NIX, and has over 3(three) prestigious research publications to his credit.
10. Moreover, he submits that during his service career there was no adverse or negative remark in his annual confidential report; thus, having an unblemished record of service and having remarkable achievements and accomplishments during his service career in the Academy he was entitled to be considered for promotion to the post of Joint Director.
11. In the given context, failure of the respondent Nos.1-4 to promote the petitioner and at the same time by giving promotion to respondent Nos.5-9 vide the impugned order dated 6-8-2019(Annexure D) upon superseding the petitioner in particular respondent No.5 who was appointed in the post of Deputy Director at the age of 42 years in violation of the Service Regulations, 1990 and 2015 respectively, is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect.
12. Conversely, Mr Shihab Uddin Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 2-4 by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary-affidavit to the affidavit-in-opposition submits that seniority in service is not the only criteria to get promotion to the higher post. In this regard, referring to the Service Regulations, 1990 as well as 2015 respectively he goes to submit that vide Regulation 11(1) and (2) of the Regulations, 2015 no one can claim promotion as of right showing seniority but is subject to the conditions as prescribed in the respective Service Regulations. In this regard, he goes to argue that the DPC in its meeting dated 4-8-2019 upon scrutinizing the merit, seniority, experience, publications, annual confidential reports etc. of the recommended candidates had finally confirmed 6(six) candidates for promotion to the post of Joint Director against 8(eight) vacant substantive posts. In this connection, he further goes to submit that the DPC did not find eligible candidates other than those 6(six) candidates; hence, the contention of the petitioner of giving promotion to respondent Nos. 5-9 upon superseding the petitioner, is absolutely misconceived and devoid of any substance; as such, not tenable in the eye of law.
13. He also submits that in the DPC meeting dated 4-8-2019 another recommended candidate named Md Mazharul Anwar, who is senior to the petitioner, was also not confirmed for the post of Joint Director whereas another candidate named Maksud Alam Khan, who is senior to the petitioner got promotion to the post of Joint Director. Accordingly, he submits that the DPC had tried to promote the best candidates amongst the recommended candidates; hence, question of arbitrariness, as alleged by the petitioner, has no leg to stand.
14. Further, drawing attention to the resolution dated 4-8-2019 (Annexure 2 to the affidavit-in-opposition) he submits that admittedly against 8(eight) substantive vacant posts of Joint Director 9(nine) candidates including the petitioner were considered for promotion. However, prior to giving recommendation for promotion the DPC considered seniority, experience, research publication, Annual Confidential Report etc. Ultimately, the name of 6(six) candidates were recommended for promotion. However, the name of the petitioner could not be considered for "“ব্যক্তিগত নথি গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদন (এসিআর) পর্যালোচনা ও চাকুরীকাল সন্তোষজনক নাহওয়ায়।”
15. In this connection, he further goes to submit that on 6-11-2013, the petitioner had also been served with a show cause notice for being negligent in performing his official duties as in charge of the Computer section. The petitioner gave reply to the said notice stating, inter-alia, “এজন্য আমি আন্তরিকভাবে দুঃখিত, মর্মাহত ও ক্ষমা প্রার্থী। সেই সাথে এই মর্মে উল্লেখ করছি যে, ভবিষ্যতে নিজ দায়িত্ব পালনে আমি আরও সচেষ্ট হব।”. Again, he submits, on 10-6-2019 another show cause notice was served upon the petitioner for being negligent in discharging his respective responsibilities. The petitioner gave reply to the said show cause notice stating, inter-alia, “তাই এমতাবস্থায়, বিনীত প্রার্থনা এই যে, দাখিলকৃত পত্রটি আপনার কারণ স্পষ্টিকরণ এবং বিষয়টি ক্ষমা সুন্দর দৃষ্টিতে দেখার জন্য মহোদয়ের সদয় মর্জি হয়।”. The authority although was not satisfied with the said reply but because of seeking apology in his reply the allegation so was brought against him was ultimately disposed off asking him to be more careful in future while discharging his respective duties.
16. Lastly, he submits that recently in the DPC meeting dated 22-12-2022 the respondent Nos. 2 and 4 had discussed the matter of the petitioner for considering his promotion to the post of Joint Director and accordingly, opined, inter-alia, that due to pendency of this Rule and ad interim order it is difficult to proceed with his promotion. Accordingly, the petitioner gave an undertaking to the authority concerned for non prosecution of the instant Rule (Annexure 12 to the affidavit-in-opposition).
17. In view of the above facts and circumstances and position of law, he submits that the instant Rule being devoid of any substance is liable to be discharged.
18. Ms. Nishat Mahmood, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.9 by filing separate set of affidavit-in-opposition adopts the submissions so have been advanced on behalf of the respondent Nos. 2 and 4 and submits that the petitioner having failed to substantiate any of the grounds/contentions this Rule is liable to be discharged.
19. Bogura Palli Unnayan Academy also, known as Rural Development Academey (RDA) has been established vide section 3 of the “বগুড়া পল্লী উন্নয়ন একাডেমী আইন, ১৯৯০” (Act No.10 of 1990) (in short, Act, 1990). Section 7, however, provides its respective responsibilities and functions which includes training, research etc. for rural development. It also provides advisory services to the government and other government organization on rural development. However, vide section 12(2) the terms and conditions of service of its officers and employees are being governed by the Regulations so made by the government under section 21 of the said Ain namely, “বগুড়া পল্লী উন্নয়ন একাডেমী কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯০” (in short, Regulations 1990) . Vide clause 6 of the Schedule of the said Regulations the post of the Deputy Director shall be filled up 50% by direct recruitment having requisite qualifications i.e. “পিএইচডি ডিক্রী অথবা স্নাতক পর্যায়ে সম্মানসহ মাধ্যমিক থেকে স্নাতকোত্তর পর্যন্ত সকল পরীক্ষায় কমপক্ষে ২য় শ্রেণীসহ ৫ বছরের চাকুরী অভিজ্ঞতা এবং ২টি গবেষণা প্রকাশনার অধিকারী হইতে হইবে।” and 50% by promotion having “সহকারী পরিচালক হিসাবে কমপক্ষে ৫ বৎসরের অভিজ্ঞতা উল্লেখযোগ্য পেশাগত খ্যাতি সহ ২টি গবেষণা প্রকাশনার অধিকারী।”
20. The petitioner having required qualifications were initially appointed in the post of Assistant Director in the Academy, who joined in his respective post on 10-11-2004. Subsequently, considering his satisfactory performance he was promoted to the post of Deputy Director on 1-4-2012 (Annexure B).
21. Conversely, from Annexure 5 to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent Nos.2 and 4 it appears that respondent No.5 was appointed by the Academy on 19-7-2022 (Annexure 5 of the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No.2) as the departmental candidate following the appointment circular published in "Daily Koratoa" on 17-10-2011 and "Daily lttefaq" on 22-10-2011 (Annexure 3) respectively. However, considering his outstanding qualifications, 15(fifteen) years working experience with RDA, Bogura the Academy in its “বগুড়া পল্লী উন্নয়ন একাডেমীর রাজস্বে খাতমুক্ত প্রথম শ্রেণীর কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগের নিমিত্তে সংশ্লিষ্ট বাছাই কমিটির” meeting dated 7-5-2012 had relaxed his age bar in view of clause (4) of the appointment circular dated 22-10-2011 (Annexure 3) which states, inter-alia, “দরখাস্ত গ্রহণের শেষ তারিখে প্রার্থীর বয়স প্রতিটি পদের বিপরীতে উল্লিখিত বয়সসীমার মধ্যে থাকতে হবে। তবে এ একাডেমীর বিভাগীয় প্রার্থীদের ক্ষেত্রে বয়সসীমা শিথিলযোগ্য।”. So far respondent 6 is concerned, she joined in the post of Deputy Director on 19-7-2012 under direct recruitment having required qualifications and work experience of 5(five) years in different reputed organizations; respondent Nos.7, 8 and 9 joined in the respective posts in the Academy on 17-11-2004, 27-2-2005 and 17-11-2004 respectively by direct recruitment.
22. Grievance of the petitioner is that vide the impugned Memo dated 6-8-2019 (Annexure D) all those respondents have been given promotion to the post of Joint Director upon superseding him despite being junior to him. In support of the said assertion the contention of the petitioner -is that respondent No.5 was age barred at the time of his initial appointment in the post of Deputy Director and respondent No. 6 did not have required service period, for, in view of clause (6) of the Schedule of the “ বগুড়া পল্লী উন্নয়ন একাডেমী কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯০” for being appointed by direct recruitment in the post of Deputy Director along with required educational qualifications, the aspiring candidate aged 35(thirty five) years has to have 5(five) years service experience with 2(two) research publications.
23. As has been observed earlier, the Academy while giving appointment to respondent No.5 as a departmental candidate on 19-7-2012 in the post of Deputy Director relaxed his age bar in the respective meeting dated 7-5-2012 under clause (4) of the appointment circular dated 22-10-2011 considering his outstanding qualifications and 15(fifteen) years service experience. Moreover, respondent No.6 was appointed and joined in the post of Deputy Director with more than 5(five) years service experience.
24. However, in view of clause (3) of the Schedule of the Service Regulations, 2015 for promotion to the post of Joint Director the candidate has to fulfill the following requirements-
“পদোন্নতির ক্ষেত্রে:
(ক) উপ-পরিচালক বা প্রটোকল অফিসার পদে অন্যূন ৫ (পাঁচ) বৎসরের চাকুরিসহ মোট ১০ (দশ) বৎসরের চাকুরি; এবং
(খ) সংশ্লিষ্ট পেশাগত খ্যাতিসহ ৩টি গবেষণা প্রকাশনা থাকিতে হইবে।
সরাসরি নিয়োগের ক্ষেত্রেঃ
(ক) কোন স্বীকৃত বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় হইতে পিএইচডি ডিগ্রী; অথবা
(খ) কোন স্বীকৃত বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় হইতে স্বাতক (ম্নাতক) বা সমমানের ডিগ্রী;
(গ) মাধ্যমিক থেকে স্নাতকোত্তর পর্যন্ত সকল পরীক্ষায় অন্যুন দ্বিতীয় শ্রেণী বা সমমানের সিজিপিএ; এবং
(ঘ) ১০ (দেশ) বৎসরের চাকুরির অভিজ্ঞতাসহ ৩টি গবেষণা প্রকাশনা থাকিতে হইবে।”
25. In the meeting of DPC dated 4-8-2019 (Annexure 2) the name of the petitioner along with 8(eight) other candidates including respondent Nos.5-9 were considered against 8(eight) vacant posts admitting the fact that the petitioner is senior to those respondents.
26. However, Regulation 11 of the Regulations, 2015 in this regard provides as under:
“১১ । পদোন্নতি।– (১) তফসিলের বিধানাবলী সাপেক্ষে, কোন কর্মচারীকে পরবর্তী উচ্চতর পদে পদোন্নতির জন্য বিবেচনা করা যাইতে পারে।
(২) কেবলমাত্র জ্যেষ্ঠতার কারণে কোন ব্যক্তি না।
(৩) টাকা ৩৭০০-৪৮-২৫ তদুর্ব বেতনক্রমের পদসমূহে পদোন্নতি মেধা তথা জ্যেষ্ঠতার ভিত্তিতে হইবে।
(8) কোন কর্মচারীকে তাহার অসাধারণ কৃতিত্ব, কর্তব্যনিষ্টা এবং চাকুরিকালে উচ্চতর পদের জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় পেশাগত পরীক্ষায় উত্তীণ হওয়ার কারণে ব্যতিক্রমী ক্ষেত্র হিসাবে, পালা অতিক্রম করতঃ পদোন্নতি দেওয়া যাইতে পারে।”
27. It is, thus, apparent that being a senior will not go to create a right to promotion, but is subject to the requirements as provided in the Schedule of the Regulations along with merit, experience, research publication, annual confidential report etc. 28. Respondent Nos.5-9 along with another having fulfilled“…..জ্যেষ্ঠতা তালিকার ক্রম ও দক্ষতা এবং বিশেষ যোগ্যতা অনুযায়ী যুগ্ম-পরিচালক পদে পদোন্নতির সকল শর্ত পূরণ করায়” DPC recommended their names for promotion. The name of the petitioner, however, was not considered on the following count: “ব্যক্তিগত নথি, বার্ষিক গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদন (এসিআর) পর্যালোচনা ও চাকুরীকাল সন্সোষজনক না হওয়ায়…..”

29. Considering the said context, the assertions of the petitioner that he has been superseded while giving promotion the respondent Nos.5-9, falls through.
30. At this juncture, admitting the facts that at the time of considering the promotion of the petitioner on 4-8-2019 (Annexure 2) there were some adverse remarks in his ACR for the year 2017 and 2018 respectively, but those were removed subsequently by the authority concerned vide Memo dated 13-12-2022 (Annexure J and J-1 respectively).
31. In view of the said assertion of the petitioner, we have examined Annexures- J and J-1 of the supplementary-affidavit. It, however, appears thereform that respective adverse remarks for the year 2017 and 2018 respectively having not been endorsed in the respective ACR in compliance with the applicable rules and regulations, were not considered by the authority concerned and accordingly, the petitioner was relieved from the respective allegations.
32. Relevant part is quoted below:-
“এমতাবস্থায় আপনার জবাব, প্রতিস্বাক্ষরকারী কর্মকর্তার মতামত ও বার্ষিক গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদনে বিরুপ মন্তব্যের বিষয়ে একাডেমীর বিদ্যমান এসিআর নীতিমালা-২০১২ ও "বার্ষিক গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদন ফরম পুরণ, অনুস্বাাক্ষরলিখন, প্রতিস্বাক্ষর ও সংরক্ষণ সংক্রান্ত অনুশাসনমালা” স্বারক নং- ০৫.১০২.২২.০১.০০.০০১.২০১২-৫৮, তারিখঃ ২৩-৯-২০১২ এবং একাডেমী’র প্রবিধানমালা-২০১৫ এর ৩৩(২) পর্যালোচনায় প্রতীয়মান হয়, বিরুপ মন্তব্য লিপিবদ্ধের ক্ষেত্রে এসিআর সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রচলিত বিধি-বিধান অনুসৃত হয়নি বিধায় উল্লিখিত বিরুপ মন্তব্যটি গ্রহণযোগ্য হিসেবে বিবেচিত না হওয়ায় আপনাকে ২০১৭ সালের এসিআর-এ বিরুপ মন্তব্যের অভিযোগ হতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করা হলো।” (Annexure J)
“এমতাবস্থায় আপনার জবাব, প্রতিস্বাক্ষরকারী কর্মকর্তার মতামত ও বার্ষিক গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদনে বিরুপ মন্তব্যের বিষয়ে একাডেমীর বিদ্যমান এসিআর নীতিমালা-২০১২ ও "বার্ষিক গোপনীয় প্রতিবেদন ফরম পুরণ, অনুস্বাাক্ষরলিখন, প্রতিস্বাক্ষর ও সংরক্ষণ সংক্রান্ত অনুশাসনমালা” স্বারক নং- ০৫.১০২.২২.০১.০০.০০১.২০১২-৫৮, তারিখঃ ২৩-৯-২০১২ এবং একাডেমী’র প্রবিধানমালা-২০১৫ এর ৩৩(২) পর্যালোচনায় প্রতীয়মান হয়, বিরুপ মন্তব্য লিপিবদ্ধের ক্ষেত্রে এসিআর সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রচলিত বিধি-বিধান অনুসৃত হয়নি বিধায় উল্লিখিত বিরুপ মন্তব্যটি গ্রহণযোগ্য হিসেবে বিবেচিত না হওয়ায় আপনাকে ২০১৮ সালের এসিআর-এ বিরুপ মন্তব্যের অভিযোগ হতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করা হলো।” (Annexure J-1)
33. Except the adverse remarks so made in the ACR for 2017 and 2018 respectively which have now been removed by the Academy for not being endorsed in due compliance of law, the respondent Academy has annexed 2 (two) show cause notices; one, on 6-11-2013 (Annexure 6) and another, on 10-6-2019 (Annexure 8). In both the cases, the petitioner replied with unconditional apology. However, the show cause notice dated 10-6-2019 was issued on the count “নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারী একাডেমীতে যোগদানের পরপরই একাডেমীর সর্বস্তরের কর্মকর্তা-কর্মচারীদের পরিচয়পত্র তৈরী করে সরবরাহের দায়িত্ব আপনাকে প্রদান করা হয়। কিন্তু ইতোমধ্যেই দীর্ঘদিন (প্রায় তিন মাস) অতিবাহিত হওয়া সত্বেও পরিচয়পত্র তৈরী ও সরবরাহের কাজটি আপনি সম্পন্ন করেননি যা দায়িত্ব অবহেলার সামিল।” Said matter was ultimately disposed of on 28-8-2019 (Annexure 10) with the following remarks “পর্যালোচনান্তে আপনার দাখিলকৃত জবাব কর্তৃপক্ষ সন্তোষজনক নয় মর্মে বিবেচিত হলেও জবাবে আপনি ক্ষমা প্রার্থনা করায় আপনার প্রতি নমনীয় মনোভাব পোষণ করতঃ ভবিষ্যতে দায়িত্ব পালনে আরও যত্নবান হওয়ার জন্য আপনাকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করে বিষয়টি নিষ্পত্তি করা হলো।”.
<u>34. Since at the relevant time i.e., on 4-8-2019 (Annexure 2) when the meeting of DPC was held and his case was being considered for promotion, there was a proceeding pending against him in connection with the show cause notice dated 10-6-2019 (Annexure 8), which has been disposed of on 28-8-2019 (Annexure 10) i.e. subsequent to passing the impugned order of promotion dated 6-8-2019 (Annexure D). As such, it cannot be said that the Academy while considering the promotion of the petitioner along with others has committed any illegality by not giving promotion to him for the post of Joint Director.</u>
35. Fact remains, now there is no proceeding pending against him and he fulfils all other requirements as prescribed under the respective Service Regulations. Under the circumstances, now, the Academy while considering the promotion of the petitioner may in its wisdom and exercising its discretionary power look into the matter of giving retrospective effect from 6-8-2019 (Annexure D).
36. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the observations so made above it is categorically found that:
(a) While giving promotion to respondent Nos.5-9 vide the impugned order dated 6-8-2019 (Annexure D) the Academy did not supersede the petitioner;
(b) Admitting the fact that the petitioner is senior to respondent Nos. 5-9, but considering his service record including ACR the Academy did not consider his promotion; High Court Division (Special Original Jurisdiction)
(c) Considering outstanding performance and 15 (fifteen) years work experience in the respective field of the Academy respondent No.5 was appointed in the post of Deputy Director relaxing the his bar vide clause (4) of the circular dated 22-10-2011 (Annexure 3); hence is found lawful;
(d) Giving promotion to respondent No.6 to the post of Joint Director having served 5 (five) years in the post of Deputy Director with more than 5 (five) years service experience while giving appointment in the post of Deputy Director, in total, having 10 years service period, is found lawful; and
(e) Last but not the least, since adverse remarks so made against the petitioner in his ACR for the year 2017 and 2018 respectively, were not done in due compliance of the respective Rules and regulation and now, are withdrawn; hence, the petitioner is now entitled to be considered for promotion to the post of Joint Director in due compliance of law.
37. With the above observations and directions, this Rule is accordingly disposed of.
There will be no order as to costs.
Communicate the judgment and order to the respondents concerned at once.
End.

lawyer:
Sharif Ahmed, Advocate—Defendant-Petitioner. 
Shammi Akter, Advocate—For the Opposite-Party Nos. 2 & 3.
parties:
Zahanara Begum --------- Defendant-Petitioner
vs
Raju Nessa being dead her legal heirs Rahela Khatun being dead her legal heirs Jhorna Begum and others -------- Plaintiff-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 16-5-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Pabna in Other Class Appeal No. 206 of 1994 affirming those dated 10-11-1994 (decree signed on 27-5-2015) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Pabna in Other Class Suit No. 26 of 1993 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. Material facts of the case, briefly, are that one, Raju Nessa (now dead), the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff opposite party No.1 and others filed Other Class Suit No. 26 of 1993 before the learned SeniOr Assistant Judge, Iswardi, Pabna impleading the petitioner as defendant praying the following' reliefs:
(ক) তপশীল ভূমি বাবদ নালিশী (খ) তপশীল দান পত্র দলিল জাল, ভূয়া, তঞ্চকী, যোগসাজসী অন্যায় অবৈধ ফল বল মূল্যহীন তাহা বাদিনীর উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে ঘোষণার ডিক্রী দিতে;
(খ) ডিত্রীর অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট DR অফিসে প্রেরণ
(গ) যাবতীয় আদালত ব্যায়াদী বাবদ বাদিনীর অনুকূলে বিবাদীনির বিরুদ্ধে খরচার ডিক্রী দিতে;
(ঘ) আইন ও ইকুইটি মূলে বাদিনী অন্য আর যে যে প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার এবং অধিকারী তাহাও বাদিনীকে ডিক্রী দিতে মর্জি হয়।
3. The plaintiff case in short is that the plaintiff, Raju Nessa owned and possessed the suit land under Mouza-Payerakhali, P.S. Iswardi by way of registered deed No. 3403 dated 27-3-1961 and she is still enjoying the possession of the suit land by constructing a house with paying the rent and the RS Khatian has been correctly prepared in her name. In this backdrop on 10-3-1993 the defendant by showing a registered deed of gift informed to the plaintiff that she gifted the schedule (Ka) land to the defendant by the said registered deed of gift and then the plaintiff became astonished and thereafter, the plaintiff collected the certified copy of the said deed executed on 21-4-1990 through her relative and having read the deed she confirmed that the defendant created a forged deed in respect of schedule (Kha) land of the plaint. The plaintiff never executed the gift deed to the defendant and never handed over the possession of the suit land to the defendant. The plaintiff never went to the Iswardi Sub-Registry office for executing the disputed deed. It is also contended that when the plaintiff became ill in the first half of Baishak of 1397 BS then the defendant (daughter of the plaintiff) and her husband brought the plaintiff in the Iswardi Hospital by Rickshaw-van for treatment and kept her in front of a building and thereafter the husband of defendant-petitioner told the plaintiff that he brought a compounder of a famous doctor with him and to collect medicine it was needed her finger print on some stamp and white papers kept in the hands of the said compounder. The plaintiff on good faith put her thump impression on those papers. Thereafter, the Doctor of that compounder came to the house of the plaintiff to see her while the doctor informed her that his compounder did not ask for any finger print or signature. The defendant and her husband in this way manipulated the forged deed of gift and hence, the suit.
4. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material averments made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the heba deed No. 1710 was registered in accordance with law and after registration of the same the plaintiff handed over the possession of the suit land to the defendant. The plaintiff filed the case on false averments and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
5. At the trial both the parties led evidence both oral and documentary to prove their respective cases.
6. The trial Court after hearing the argument of both parties and on considering the materials on record by its judgment and decree dated 10-11-1994 decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff.
7. The defendant No 1, thereupon, preferred Other Class Appeal No. 206 of 1994 before the learned District Judge, Pabna, which was eventually transmitted to the Court of the learned Joint District judge, 1st Court, Pabna for disposal, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 16-5-2002 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
8. Aggrieved defendant then preferred this Revision application and obtained the present rule.
9. Mr Sharif Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner submits that both the Courts below having failed to consider that the deed of heba was registered in accordance with law on 21-4-1990 and on the same date the possession of suit land was handed over by the plaintiff and since then the defendant-petitioner has been residing on the suit land by erecting a house and thereby erroneously decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff.
10. Ms. Shammi Akter, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-party Nos. 2-3, on the other hand, supports the judgments of both the Courts below, which were according to him just, correct and proper.
11. I have considered the submission of the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the Civil Revision application, judgments of two courts below and other papers.
12. In this case, the only question for consideration is , whether the trial Court and the appellant Court below correctly held in the facts and circumstances of the case that the plaintiff has been succeeded to prove her case and the deed of gift dated 21-4-1990 is not binding upon the plaintiff.
13. On scrutiny of the record, it is found that in this case the plaintiff herself was examined as PW-1, who in her deposition stated that-
“আমার সাড়ে চার বৎসর আগে বৈশাখ মাসে অসুখ হইয়াছিল । আমার মেয়ে জামাই অর্থাৎ ১নং বিবাদী ও তাহার স্বামী আমাকে চিকিৎসার নাম করিয়া হাসপাতালে নিয়া যান এবং সেখানে আমার মেয়ে জামাই সাদা কাগজে টিপ সহি নিয়া নেয় এবং কিছু ঔষধ দেন (with objection). আমার বাড়িতে আমি এখনও বসবাস করিতেছি । আমি ১নং বিবাদীকে দান করিতে চাই নাই । আমার মেয়ে জামাই আমাকে কখনও দলিল পড়িয়া শুনাই নাই বা কেহ আমাকে দলিল পড়িয়া শুনাই নাই। উক্ত দলিলের সাক্ষ্য সনাক্তকারী কাহাকেও চিনি না । This witness also stated that- “নাঃ জমি ছাড়া আমার আর জমি নাই এবং আমার দুইটা মেয়ে মাত্র এবং আমার ছেলে নাই । আমার মেয়ে ১নং বিবাদী ও তাহার স্বামী ও দলিল লেখকেরা যোগসাজসে দলিল. সৃষ্টি করেন । নাঃ দলিলটি আমার উপর বাধ্যকর নহে ও বাতিল মর্মে ঘোষণামূলক ডিক্রীর প্রার্থনা করিতেছি।”. PW 2, Bahar Uddin as close relative of plaintiff in his evidence corroborated the evidence of PW 1 in respect of all material particulars.
14. From the evidence of PW 1 and PW 2 it appears that the plaintiff did not execute the heba deed in question which was obtained on practicing fraud on her and she never handed over the possession of the suit land to the defendant.
15. Now, let me advert to the evidence of DWs. Defendant No.1 herself was examined as DW 1, who stated in her deposition that the plaintiff voluntarily executed the gift deed in her favour and on the date of registration the
possession of the suit land was handed over to her. This witness also stated in her deposition that-
“দান দলিলটি আমার মায়ের কথামত লিখা হইয়াছিল এবং দান লিখার পর পড়িয়া শুনানোর পরে আমার মা দলিলে টিপ দিয়া সম্পাদন করেন। নাঃ জমি আমি রেজিদ্টরির দিন থেকেই দখল করিতেছি । নাঃ জমিতে বাড়ীঘর করিয়া বসবাস করিতেছি । নাঃ জমি আমার মা দানের পর থেকে আর দখল করে না।”
16. DW-2 and DW-3 in their respective evidence stated that the mother of the defendant No. 1 herself voluntarily executed the deed in favour of the defendant No.1 and also handed over the possession of the suit land to the defendant No. 1.
17. It is found that in this case the Deed Writer was not examined. On a close perusal of the PWs and DWs, it appears that the evidence of DWs as to execution of the deed and handing over the possession of the suit land is not free from doubt. Weighing the evidence of both the parties, I find that the evidence in plaintiff side is credible and tenable in Law The trial Court as first Court of fact on due consideration of the entire evidence and materials on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiff has been succeeded to prove her case by adducing reliable evidence and the that deed of gift dated 21.4.1990 is not binding upon the plaintiff.
18. The Court of appeal below as last Court of fact in its turn observed as follows:
“ফলতঃ সামগ্রীক ভাবে বলা যায় যে, নালিশী দানপত্র দলিলটি বাদিনী স্বেচ্ছায় ও স্বজ্ঞানে ১নং বিবাদীনির বরাবরে সম্পাদিন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করে দেননি । বাদীনিকে ভুল বুঝিয়ে চিকিৎসার নাম করে সাব রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে নিয়ে গিয়ে বাদীনির টিপ সহি হাসিল করে তর্কিত দানপত্র দলিল করে নেয়া হয় । নালিশী দানপত্র দলিলটি যোগসাজসী এবং তঞ্চকতামূলক । বাদীনি স্বেচ্ছায় ও স্বজ্ঞানে ১নং বিবাদীনি বরাবর উক্ত দানপত্র দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করে না দেয়ায় উত্ত দলিলটি একটি অকার্যকরী দলিল।”
19. This finding certainly indicates that the learned Joint District Judge, Pabna considered all the material aspects of the case and justly recorded the order of rejection.
<u>20. Generally, it is the duty of the party to lead the best evidence to prove the genuineness of the deed in question, which could throw light on the issue in controversy and in case such material witness (deed writer) is withheld, the Court may draw adverse inference under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act that the evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavorable to the party who withholds it.</u>
<u>21. Law is well settled that a finding of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court is binding upon the High Court Division in Revision except in certain well-defined circumstances such as non-consideration and misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case and in the present case the judgments of 2 Courts below are well based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case and, as such, question of interference does not arise at all.</u>
22. By the way, it may be observed that as per evidence and materials on record the plaintiff's only homestead situated on the suit land and plaintiff's has/had no other land, plaintiff is mother of 2 daughters and thus, I find no believable reason to hold the plaintiff voluntarily executed the deed in question dated 21-4-1990 in favour of one daughter (defendant No. 1). Therefore, I find no reason to differ with the view taken by the Courts below. Both the Courts below appear to have considered all the material aspects of the case and justly decreed the suit. No interference is, therefore, called for.
23. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.
Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Courts' record be sent down at once.
End.

Government of the People's Republic of- Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka....   Defendant-Appellant
vs
Hazi Md Alek Mia and 24th January, 2024. Others  ......Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: Defendants 1-3 have preferred this appeal against judgment and decree dated 10-2-2019 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 117 of 2017 decreeing the suit.
2. Suit was filed on 13-2-2017 for declaration of title and for further declaration that the RS and City Survey records prepared in The name of the defendants are wrong.
3. The case of the plaintiffs is that the CS tenants and their successive heirs in whose names SA record also stands sold 0.49 acres out of 0.55 acres from plot 447 and 0.49 acres out of 0.55 acres from plot 448 to Arab Ali, Romizuddin, Motaleb Fakir, Moyezuddin by registered kabala dated 19-2-1965 and inducted them into possession. The suit land measuring 0.98 acres is a pond in which purchasers maintain joint possession by rearing fish. They while trying to transfer the same came to learn on 5-12-2016 that the suit land was not recorded in their names and upon collecting the printed copies of RS and City Survey records on 22-1-2017 and 23-1-2017 they came to know that those were wrongly prepared in the name of defendant 1. Hence the suit was filed.
4. The contention of defendants 1-3 is that the suit is barred by limitation and 0.76 acres of CS and SA plots 447, 448 corresponding to RS plots 952, 953 as well as City Survey plots 2024, 2025 are correctly prepared in the name of defendant 1 in khas khatian 1 in which defendant 1 maintain possession and control. Plaintiffs have no title and interest in the suit pond. Suit was filed with malafide intention to grab the pond. The suit being false is liable to be dismissed.
5. The lower Court framed as many as five issues as to maintainability; limitation; whether plaintiffs have title, interest, right and possession in the suit property; whether the RS record and City Survey record have been wrongly prepared in the name of defendant 1 in respect of the suit property; whether plaintiffs can get the relief as prayed for.
6. During the course of trial plaintiffs examined 2(two) witnesses and defendants examined 1(one) witness and both the parties adduced documentary evidence in order to prove their respective cases.
7. The Joint District Judge decreed the suit on 10-2-2019 on the finding that the suit is not barred by limitation and plaintiffs have acquired title by purchase and PW 2 supported possession and further found that since transfer was made in favour of plaintiffs before RS operation the subsequent records prepared in the name of defendant 1 are wrong and defence failed to prove the basis of the record so prepared.
8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment passed by the Joint District Judge defendants preferred the instant appeal before this Court.
9. Ms Apurba Kumar Bhattacharjee, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the Court below erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and decree upon wrongful consideration and failed to apply its judicial mind. The impugned decree was passed upon mere surmise and conjecture and Court failed to reach to a correct conclusion. He further submits that plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession in the suit pond by adducing proper and lawful evidence. Court failed to consider that weakness of defense is no ground for granting decree in favour of plaintiffs. He submits that the alleged true copy of the deed dated 19-2-1965 is a forged deed created by the plaintiffs showing the same registered in the office of sub-registrar, Islamkati, Khulna which was burnt into ashes.
10. Ms Sadekur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf the respondents submits that the Joint District Judge upon proper appreciation of evidence and law has correctly decreed the suit. He then submits that the finding of the trial Court that plaintiffs have proved their title and possession in the suit property is based on evidence and since the impugned decree is lawfully passed the same is immuned from interference in appeal.
11. We have heard the learned Advocates of both sides and perused all the materials on record and gone through the impugned judgment and the grounds taken in appeal.
12. Plaintiffs filed the suit on the strength of kabala dated 19-2-1965 claiming as transferees from the CS and SA tenants. The true copy of the kabala which is certified by sub-registrar, Islamkati, Khulna on 25-5-1966 with a heading of words like "residential certificate issued by First Class Magistrate duly submitted Khulna" was tendered by the plaintiffs in evidence and marked as Exhibit-9. The document was produced by PW-1 on 13-8-2018 who is plaintiff No. 8 in the snit and the same was admitted without objection. PW 1 was examined on commission on behalf of all the plaintiffs by virtue of a power of attorney, Exhibit-1 dated 26-7-2018. The suit was tiled on 13-2-2017. In the plaint there is no explanation as to why the original of the document could not be filed. Law says that when a party desires to prove a document the best evidence rule requires that the party should produce the original of the primary evidence under section 62 of the Evidence Act. But if he fails to meet such requirement he can file a certified copy of the same under sections 63 and 65 of the Evidence Act and in such a case it is his duty to explain away in his pleading and evidence as to why he failed to produce the original. In the instant case pleading and evidence do not say so. Law is settled that a party producing 'a secondary evidence of a document is not exempted from explaining why the original could not be produced even though no objection was raised when it was tendered and marked in evidence. It seems that the writing on Exhibit-9 has been lately done on old stamp papers, The document was not at all proved in evidence because either the executants or their descendants or any scribe, attesting witness, identifier came before the Court to -prove the same. Moreover Exhibit-9 shows that the second schedule of the document contains 0.08 acres of land of Police Station Tala of Islamkati sub-registry office of District Khulna but plaint is silent about it and respondents could not submit any document showing the property mentioned in 2nd schedule to the deed belonged to the vendors. Thus it is clear that the document contains fictitious land and is an invalid document being barred under section 28 of the Registration Act. It also appears from perusing the seal given on the reverse side of the second page of the document that the copy was prepared, sealed, signed and delivered on 23-5-1966 but on the last page the date is 25-5-1966. The document was prepared on 25-5-1966 but read over by a person on 27-4-1965. Moreover it is detected with the naked eye that the signatures of sub-registrar differ from each other. The stamps used in the deed have no number at the back side and serious anomalies led us to believe that the deed is forged and fictitious one. We have asked the learned Advocate for the respondent as to why the deed was shown to be registered in the office of sub-registrar, Islamkati, Khulna where there is no averment in the pleading in respect of schedule-2 property but he failed to reply to satisfaction. All those facts and circumstances clearly establish that the deed in question has been manufactured by the plaintiffs in suit. Similarly, another group of people came with an application for addition of party as respondents by showing a true copy of the sale deed. On scrutiny and calling volume from the sub-registry office, Tejgaon it was found that the same was forged one and consequently application was rejected imposing penalty and directing the District Registrar, Dhaka to file criminal case. Exhibit-9 as has been discussed above is a fake, forged, fraudulent document and the same does not confer any title to the plaintiffs. Since plaintiffs failed to prove their title they are not entitled to challenge the subsequent record of rights prepared in the name of defendant 1 under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and such records bear presumptive value under section 144(A) of the same Act and cannot be dislodged until found incorrect.
13. Paragraph 6 of the plaint shows that the suit land is pond in nature in which plaintiffs have been maintaining possession by rearing fish. In chief PW 1 also stated the same. Neither plaint nor evidence discloses as to how and by whom such possession was maintained by the plaintiffs. PW 1 admitted in cross that they have not paid rent after the suit land was recorded in RS khatian. The revisional survey was completed in the concerned area before 1976. Plaintiffs even did not file any rent-receipt showing earlier payment since their purchase or by their transferors. PW 2 admittedly lives in a different place and his evidence is not sufficient to prove possession of the plaintiffs being unconvincing and incredible. Plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove their possession in the suit land. Exhibits 10, 11, Kha, Ga are good evidence of possession of defendant 1 and the presumption of such entry in the name of defendant is never dislodged by any cogent and reliable evidence.
<u>14. The instant case falls under sections 101-103 of the Evidence Act. Plaintiffs vant the Court to believe that the kabala Exhibit-9 is a genuine document but as discussed above this Court found the same as fake, forged, fabricated and invalid. Plaintiffs failed to discharge their initial onus on proving title and possession in the suit land. Exhibits- Kha, Ga, 10, 11 show that defendant 1 has got possession in the suit land. Plaintiffs having failed to prove their title are not entitled to challenge Exhibits-Kha and Ga prepared in the name of defendant 1. The Joint District Judge misconceived the law and facts of the case and arrived at a wrong conclusion and the-impugned judgment and decree being perverse are liable to be set-aside, Claim of title by plaintiff based on a forged document showing the same registered in a different sub-registry office is highly deprecated. Since we found the deed is forged and used in Court as evidence the plaintiffs are liable to be punished for committing forgery. It is to be mentioned that a group of land grabbers in collusion with the staffs and officers of the registration office are engaged in forging various sale deeds and using the same successfully manage to achieve decree from the Court and grab the Government properties which cannot be allowed to continue.</u>
15. Therefore, we find merit in the appeal and accordingly the same is allowed.
16. The impugned judgment and decree dated 10-2-2019 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 117 of 2017 is set-aside and the suit is dismissed with costs.
17. The District Registrar, Dhaka is directed to lodge a complaint under sections 468 and 471 of the Penal Code against the plaintiffs in suit.
18. Send down the lower Court's record.
19. Communicate this judgment to the concerned Court.
The deed (Exhibit-9) in question is hereby forfeited and the office is directed to retain the same. A copy of the judgment and the disputed deed be sent to the District Registrar, Dhaka for doing needful.
End.

parties:
Golum Bahauddin (Md) ------------ Petitioner
vs
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Defence and others -------Respondents
full_judgment:
Naima Haider, J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi was issued on 2-12-2015 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Memo dated 17-10-2011 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) purporting to compulsorily retire the petitioner from service and the Memo dated 21-5-2013 (Annexure-A-1 to the writ petition) purporting to refuse the petitioner's trial under the relevant law both issued by the respondent No. 5 should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why they should not be directed to pay the petitioner all back wages, house rents and allowances etc. by exonerating him from the charges of attempted rape and murder and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in brief are that: This writ petition was 'filed challenging the Impugned Memo dated 17-10-2021 and Impugned Memo dated 21-5-2013 (Annexures A and A1) issued by the Respondent No. 1, the Ministry of Defence ordering compulsory retirement of the Petitioner. A Rule Nisi was issued on 2-2-2015 in terms of the prayer by a Division Bench of the High Court Division comprising Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury and Mr Justice Ashraful Kamal.
3. The Petitioner is a former Lieutenant of Bangladesh Navy and a citizen of Bangladesh. The Petitioner successfully completed his Basic Military course from Bangladesh Naval Academy and upon serving to the full satisfaction of the relevant authorities, the Petitioner was commissioned as an officer on January 6, 2007. At all the material times, the Petitioner was the only Professional Marine Engineer in Bangladesh Navy. Since being commissioned as an officer of the Bangladesh Navy in 2007, the Petitioner served the country with sincerity, honesty, loyalty, and dedication. No allegation of misconduct or inefficiency was ever brought against him before. The Petitioner is widely recognized as one of the most successful and efficient officers of the Bangladesh Navy. The Petitioner completed his Basic Electrical Course and Basic Engineering Course which were required for Engine Room Watch Officer on board ship from BNS Shahid Moazzam; Basic Logistics and Management Course (BLMC) from BNS Titumir, Khulna; Operational Sea Training Guide from BNS Bangabandhu; Additional Sea Training on board ship BNS Osman. That the Petitioner further completed the Basic Elementary Course First Aid, Fire Fighting and Fire Prevention, Personal Safety and Social Responsibility and Personal Survival Technique from IIMT, Chittagong as per STWC' 95. The Petitioner received Work Shop and Machine Shop Certificates and he has completed 460 hours Machine Shop Course from BITAC, Dhaka and six months course on Work Shop Practice and Process. He also obtained Watch Keeping Certificate from BNS Bangabandhu (Former BNS Khaled Bin Walid) the largest Frigate of Bangladesh Navy. Duration of Sea Time was from 10-1-2008 to 15-2-2009. He also obtained Class-III FVEOC (3rd Engineer) Certificate from Department of Shipping, Government of Bangladesh. The Petitioner made several Goodwill visits aboard while he was serving the Navy. He participated in Joint Exercise "Ferocious Falcon-2008" held at Qatar, Doha, and obtained a certificate from Qatar Armed Forces. In 2008, he has done Cruise at Cochin, India on board Ship BNS Bangabandhu and also participated in Goodwill visit to Maldives on board ship BNS Bangabandhu. The Petitioner completed the Certificate Course on Financial Management, Material Management & Human Resources Management from Khulna University, Khulna. The Petitioner worked as a Contingent Commander in aid of civil power at Satkhira, Khulna in 2008. In 2009, he served as Secretary to the Commanding Officer, BNS Isa Khan and as Contingent Commander, Security at Mangla Port on 2010. He also worked as Asst OTC; NSSD, Dhaka Cantonment from 2010 to 2011 and as deputy Contingent Commander, Navy, BGB (former BDR) in 2010. All along, his official track record and performance was very good, In October 2010, he was transferred to Dhaka BNS Hazi Mohsin.
4. While the Petitioner was working there, he fell in love with his colleague, one area law officer, Instructor Lieutenant Shabnom Parvin Swapna (P No 2031). When the Petitioner proposed to marry her, she started to play a deceitful game about the marriage with him. As the Petitioner and the lady officer both were very open about their relationship, the Navy Intelligence Branch Officer in Charge (OIC), Field Intelligence Service (FIS) started to watch their movement and at one stage, they questioned both the Petitioner and the lady officer separately on 15-5-2011 and by their observation, the truth came out that the lady officer cheated with the Petitioner about marriage and she also took a lot of monetary and other facilities including commodities from the Petitioner by deceit in the name of love while they were in relationship. On 15-5-2011, OIC, FIS sent the intelligence report on it to the Director of the Naval Intelligence (DNI) and OIC, NSSD the Petitioner's senior officer. The Petitioner sought justice to his higher authorities (Admin Authority, Dhaka and Commanding Officer of BNS Hazi Mohsin) about this matter, but they did not pay any attention and also failed to handle the whole situation properly as expected. On 2-7-2011, at around 7-15 pm both the Petitioner and the lady officer had a heated conversation with each other and at one stage, the lady officer attacked the Petitioner resulting in serious injury to him. On the other hand, no sign of injury was marked on her. The lady officer created such a situation intentionally and took advantage from that situation by playing a deceitful game. After this incident, the Administrative Authority, Dhaka put the Petitioner under close arrest and seized all cellular phone sets. He was denied all facilities of communication. The Administrative Authority, Dhaka formed a Board of Enquiry, known as Naval Administrative Authority committee to enquire about the above incident. The enquiry committee accused the Petitioner of various allegations and without conducting any proper investigation recommended some severe punishment against the Petitioner. The enquiry report was never given to the Petitioner. Then on 17-10-2011, without any trial whatsoever, the Respondent No. 5 by an Impugned Order dated 17-10-2011 (Annexure A) issued an order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner thereby punishing the Petitioner, purportedly under the cloak of section 17(1) of the Navy Ordinance, 1961 ("the 1961 Ordinance") read with Regulation 801(d) of the Navy Regulations, 1981 ("the 1981 Regulations"). It was a non-speaking order, no cause or reason having been cited, amounting to termination simpliciter. The Petitioner subsequently complained to different authorities, including but not limited to the Hon'ble President and the Hon'ble Prime Minister protesting against the order of compulsory retirement.
5. On 15-4-2013, the Petitioner, through his lawyer Mr Mustafa Sarwar, 14 Court House Street, Zowaher Complex, Room No. 307, PS Kotwali, District-Dhaka, sent a legal notice to the Respondent No. 2 demanding justice (Annexure F) re his grievances according to law. In reply to the legal notice dated 15-4-2013, the Respondent No. 4 on 8-5-2013 (Annexure G), informed the Petitioner in writing to the effect that; according to Reg. 801(d) of the 1981 Regulations, the Government can make an administrative order of compulsory retirement of any Navy Officer for misconduct. Also, according to section 14(5) of the Navy Ordinance 1961, the Government can discharge any Navy Officer from his service without showing any reason. On the other hand, according to section 140 of the Navy Ordinance 1961, no Court shall question the correctness, legality or propriety of any proceeding, order, finding or sentence of any Naval Tribunal, and no appeal, revision or other remedy shall lie in respect of any such proceeding, order, finding or sentence save in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance. By citing the above mentioned reasons, the Respondents declined to reconsider the Petitioner's prayer in paragraph (Uma) of the said reply to the legal notice, the Judge Advocate General, who is the Chief law officer for Naval forces clearly admitted that although it would have been possible to convene a Court Martial against the Petitioner or take other steps to punish him, but they chose not to do so. The relevant paragraph is quoted below:
“লেঃ বাহাউদ্দিন, (এস) বিএনভিআর (পি নং ১৮৫২) এর অপরাধ এর গুরুত্ বিবেচনা করিয়া তদন্ত পর্ষদের সুপারিশের প্রেক্ষিতে তাহাকে কোর্ট মার্শাল এ বিচার করিয়া দৃষ্টান্তমূলক সাজা প্রদান কিংবা প্রশাসনিক আদেশে চাকুরী হইতে বহিষ্কার করা সম্ভব হইত কিন্তু কর্মকর্তার চাকুরীকাল, বয়স এবং সর্বোপরি তাহার ভবিষ্যৎ বিবেচনা করিয়া তাহাকে কোর্ট মার্শালে বিচার কিংবা প্রশাসনিক আদেশে চাকুরী হইতে বহিষ্কার না করিয়া প্রশাসনিক আদেশে বাধ্যতামূলক অবসর প্রদান করা হয়।”
6. The Petitioner also applied to the Respondent No. 1 for trial, reinstatement and/or compensation and was refused the same by the Impugned Order dated 21-5-2013 [Annexure A(1)] which clearly stated the connection between the Petitioner's compulsory retirement and the charges of attempted rape and attempted murder against the Petitioner, rendering the termination, termination with stigma without any chance to clear his name.
7. On 7-7-2014, the Petitioner complained (Annexure. H) to the National Human Rights Commission ("the NHRC"), Bangladesh stating his grievances and seeking remedy. Subsequently, the Respondent No. 1 sent a letter dated 8-10-2014 against the inquiry of NHRC mentioning the initial enquiry report, complaints against the Petitioner and steps taken against the Petitioner thereof. The said letter dated 8-10-2014 (Annexure I) also attached therewith a Report dated 8-10-2014 (Annexure I(1)) signed by the Respondent No.6 and a letter dated 30-9-2014 signed by the Respondent No. 4 (Annexure I(2)). It is clear from the Report that the enquiry committee, after the preliminary investigation, made three observations regarding the Petitioner. Firstly, the Respondents found the Petitioner guilty of the accusation of attempted rape, secondly, they recommended exemplary punishment for the Petitioner and finally, considering the Petitioner's service period, age, future and relationship with the lady officer and the consent of and temptation and exploitation by the lady officer, the Respondents clearly indicate that they have used the order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner as a tool of punishment on the basis of the enquiry report and presumption only thereby casting a stigma upon the Petitioner. The letter clearly stated that the Petitioner was punished on the basis of the enquiry report. As a matter of fact neither any court martial was convened nor were the allegations tried by any criminal court. The Petitioner also by his letter 18-12-2014 (Annexure J) submitted his reply to the inquiry of NHRC. NHRC, by Order No. 7 dated 8-1-2015 of Complaint No. 268 of 2014 (Annexure J(1)) made an observation to the effect that since the positions of both the sides were irreconcilable, they were advised to settle the dispute through a court of law according to the law of the land. Having no other alternative or efficacious remedy, the Petitioner filed this writ petition.
8. An Affidavit-in-Opposition was filed on behalf of the Respondent No. 4 stating as follows: The legality of the Impugned Memos are not liable to be challenged in writ jurisdiction as the Petitioner - was in service in a disciplined force as per Article 45 read with Article 134 of the Constitution.
9. The Petitioner admitted that he did not take his colleague as colleague in the service and thus violated discipline.
10. Following the occurrence that took place on 2-7-2011, the office the Naval Staff formed a four-member committee to inquire about the incident. The committee on 5-7-2011 submitted its report (Annexure 2) which revealed the real facts.
11. On 6-7-2011 a show cause notice (Annexure-3) was issued upon the Petitioner and on 7-7-2011 he replied (Annexure-4) to the show cause notice. Subsequently, the impugned notice was issued. The Petitioner was found guilty on the basis of the inquiry report which contained a confessional statement of the Petitioner. The actual causes of the impugned orders are mentioned in the reply to the legal notice (Annexure G).
12. The Petitioner is trying to tarnish the image of the Bangladesh Navy.
13. The Learned Advocates, Mr Akhtar Imam and Ms. Rashna Imam made the following submissions on behalf of the Petitioner:
The allegations against the Petitioner, that is, attempted rape and attempted murder are civil offences as defined in section 4(iii) of the Navy Ordinance and, as such, ought to have been tried by a naval tribunal as per section 78 or by a criminal court pursuant to the concurrent jurisdiction of naval tribunal and criminal court for trial of civil offences under section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and 549 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898. The Report of the Board of Inquiry (Annexure 2, Affidavit-in-Opposition) recommended harsh punishment against the Petitioner, which can only be inflicted after the trial process. The National Human Rights Commission through Order No. 7 (Annexure J(1)) disposed of the complaint lodged by the Petitioner by recommending that he should resolve the matter through the courts.
14. The Impugned Order of compulsory retirement is stated to be based on the exercise of the power under section 17(1) of the Navy Ordinance read with Regulations 0801 and 0807 of the Navy Regulations. The power of compulsory retirement of the Respondents under section 17(1) of the Navy Ordinance should only be exercised in case of misconduct, inefficiency or a reason akin to that (ejusdem generis) as explained in Regulations 0801 and 0807 of the Navy Regulations and not in a case, such as the instant case, in which the allegations against the Petitioner amount to civil offences, which warrant a trial by a Naval Tribunal as provided in section 78 of the Navy Ordinance or a criminal court under section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and 549 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898.
"0801. Circumstances in which termination of service occurs: An officer's service is terminated in any one of the following circumstances:—
…………………………………………………………………
(d) compulsory retirement or resignation, under the orders of the Government , for an officer's misconduct or any other reason."
"0807. Dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement of officers for misconduct, etc. procedure. The following procedure will be observed to deal with cases in which it is not practicable or desirable to convene a court martial for the trial of an officer against whom misconduct or inefficiency, etc. is imputed and his retention in service is not considered to be in the interest of the Navy’….
15. Article 45 of the Constitution only saves (from challenge under Article 102) law of a specific kind (namely disciplinary law, relating to members of a disciplined force, limited to the purpose of ensuring proper discharge of duties and maintenance of discipline in that force) and action authorised by such law. However, it does not save from challenge under Article 102 the following: "an action such as the Impugned Order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner in the instant case which is not authorised by the Navy Ordinance which specifically provides for trial by a naval tribunal or a criminal court in case of commission of civil offences like attempted rape and attempted murder;
Para. 2.223, Mahmudul Islam, Constitutional Law of Bangladesh, Third Edition: "Article 45 provides that no challenge on the ground of violation of fundamental rights guaranteed by Part HI will be available in respect of any provision of a disciplinary law relating to the members of a disciplined force, which is a provision limited to the purpose of ensuring the proper discharge of duties by members of the disciplined force or the maintenance of discipline in that force. Article 45 saves only a law of the specified kind and not any action. Thus where a fundamental right is violated by an action, that action shall not be immune from attack. But if the violation is authorised by a taw of the kind mentioned in Article 45, no challenge can be maintained".
16. Bangladesh & others vs AKM Zahangir Hossain, 34 DLR (AD) 173: The disciplined force in this case was the police. The court held that, "In an appropriate case when he has been illegally dismissed, removed, discharged, compulsorily retired or reduced in rank, he is entitled to invoke the writ jurisdiction under Article 102."
17. Law and/or action taken under such law that does not relate to the proper discharge of duties or maintenance of discipline in a disciplined force as in the instant case which has nothing to do with the proper discharge of duties or maintenance of discipline. Firstly, it was a personal matter between a man and a woman which has no connection with either the discharge of duties or the maintenance of discipline in the force and secondly, allegations of attempted rape and attempted murder cannot reasonably be considered to be a matter of discipline.
18. Col. Md Hashmat Ali vs Bangladesh, 47 DLR (AD) 1, para 16:
"I am of the view that a member of any disciplined force of Bangladesh will not be entitled to any remedy under Article 102 if he is aggrieved………. by any violation of fundamental right resulting from application of a disciplinary law for the purpose of ensuring the proper discharge of his duties or the maintenance of discipline in the disciplined force."
19. The Impugned Orders of compulsory retirement has deprived the Petitioner of all the protections afforded to him by the trial process, be it by a naval tribunal under section 78 of the Navy Ordinance or by a criminal court under section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and section 549 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, including but not limited to the right to object to any officer constituting court-martial (section 109), right of trial under the protection of oath by every member of the court-martial (section 110), protection of testimony of witnesses under oath (section 110), protection of rules of evidence (section 114) which includes his right to be presumed innocent until the contrary is proved beyond reasonable doubt, right to cross-examine and test the veracity of the witnesses, right of confirmation, revision and review of the findings of court-martial under Chapter XII of the Navy Ordinance, right of pardons, remissions and suspensions under Chapter XIV of the Navy Ordinance.
20. A parallel may be drawn between termination simpliciter without stigma and compulsory retirement without stigma based on the doctrine of pleasure of the president (Article 134 of the Constitution), both of which are immune from challenge, however, the instant case is one of compulsory retirement with stigma as evident from the second Impugned Order (Annexure A 1) and a host of correspondence/ reports (Annexures G, I(1), I(2), etc.) that followed the first Impugned Order of compulsory retirement and, as such, is amenable to writ jurisdiction, Article 134 being no bar. In Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation vs Md Ali Hossain, 18 MLR (AD) 265 = 65 DLR (AD) 158 the Court held in paragraph 60 that, "If the employee is guilty of any offence he may be proceeded with in accordance with the disciplinary procedure available under the rule of the said “কর্মচারী চাকরি প্রবিধানমালা, and if an employee have been found to have been involved in any offence, as in this case, the said employee may be punished even if (by) imposing the penalty available in the “প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯০”. But under no circumstances, the power of termination simpliciter can be exercised for such offence of the employee." The Court also held in paragraph 43 that, If the petitioner committed any offence in 2000-2001 as allegedly found by the enquiry committee of the corporation in its report submitted on 31-12-2001 and then again in 2006, he could be proceeded with and punished under the provisions of the Probidhanmala 1990, but in no case, he could be terminated for commission of such offences."
21. The Impugned Order of compulsory retirement was not to maintain discipline but to punish the Petitioner in the garb of compulsory retirement without a trial as required by section 78 and section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and, as such, is downright malafide and a colourable exercise of the Respondent's power under section 17(1) and, as such, the bar in Article 45 and Article 134 to invoking the writ jurisdiction does not apply to the instant case. In Cot Md Hashmat Ali vs Bangladesh 47 DLR (AD) I the court held in paragraphs 16 and 17 that,
"A member of the disciplined force can be an aggrieved person and can also move, subject to the provision of Article 45 of the Constitution, the High Court Division for enforcement of fundamental rights. There are, however, certain constitutional limitations of the judicial review of an order passed or action taken against a member of a disciplined force in this country. Reading clause (5) of Article 102, Article 134 and Article 45 of the Constitution together I am of the view that a member of any disciplined force of Bangladesh will not be entitled to any remedy under Article 102 if he is aggrieved (I) by any decision of a court or tribunal established under a law relating to the defence services unless that decision is coram non-judice or malafide; or (II) by any violation of fundamental right resulting from application of a disciplinary law for the purpose of ensuring the proper discharge of duties or maintenance of discipline in the disciplined force. This is not a case of punishment nor one of compulsory retirement that can be construed as punishment."
22. The fundamental rights of the Petitioner guaranteed under Article 27 to be treated equally before the law, under Article 31 to be treated in accordance with law and under Article 40 to pursue any lawful trade or profession have been violated by the Impugned Orders and the bar to invoking the writ jurisdiction for enforcement of such right under Article 45 does not apply in the instant case for reasons stated and submissions made hereinabove.
23. The Learned Deputy Attorney-Genera', Mr Amit Das Gupta, on behalf of the Respondent No. 4, as reflected in the Affidavit-in-Opposition submitted as follows: The legality of the Impugned Order is not liable to be challenged in writ jurisdiction.
24. The Petitioner committed some acts contrary to his service and, as such, he was given compulsory retirement.
25. Admission on the part of the Petitioner that he did not take his colleague as colleague in the service is admission of violation of discipline in the disciplined force and, as such, the impugned order was rightly passed.
26. The lawful order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner was issued following the concerned rules and regulations.
27. The Petitioner was in service in a disciplined force and, as such, pursuant to Article 45 of the Constitution he is not entitled to invoke the writ jurisdiction regarding his service matter.
28. The Petitioner was compulsorily retired by administrative action consistent with the relevant rules and regulations.
29. The actual causes of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner were mentioned in the reply of legal notice issued by the Respondent No. 4 (Judge Advocate-General, Bangladesh Navy) which is absolutely within the purview of existing laws applicable to Bangladesh Navy as well as naval personnel.
30. The members of the Defence Services of the Republic hold office during the pleasure of the President which is not subject to or controlled by any law or constitutional provision. The Petitioner has no right in respect of his service to be enforced through a court of law. The Petitioner was given compulsory retirement following due process of law.
31. We need to mention here that during the course of the submissions on behalf of the Petitioner, Mr Akhtar Imam, Senior Advocate, made a final submission to the effect that the Petitioner after so many years does not want reinstatement or back wages or any kind of compensation. All that the Petitioner prays for is complete exoneration from the charges of attempted rape and murder so that he along with his family does not have to live the rest of his/their life with such a stigma.
32. On a careful consideration of the afore-said submissions of the respective parties and after a thorough examination of the facts and law in this regard, our findings are as follows. It has been argued on behalf of the Respondent No. 4 that the writ petition is not maintainable by virtue of Article 45, the Petitioner being in service in the disciplined force. As such, the issue of maintainability needs to be addressed first, before we proceed to adjudicate the matter on merits. Article 45 in Part III of the Constitution of Bangladesh states as follows:
"Modification of rights in respect of disciplinary law. Nothing in this Part shall apply to any provision of a disciplinary law relating to members of a disciplined force, being a provision limited to the purpose of ensuring the proper discharge of their duties or the maintenance of discipline in that force."
33. In other words, the writ jurisdiction cannot be invoked on the ground of violation of fundamental rights guaranteed by Part III of the Constitution in respect of any provision of a disciplinary law relating to the members of a disciplined force. However, the provision of the" disciplinary law must be limited to the purpose of ensuring proper discharge of duties by members of the disciplined force or the maintenance of discipline in that force. As Mr Mahmudul Islam correctly points out in Paragraph 2.223 of his treatise on Constitutional Law of Bangladesh, Third Edition, Article 45 saves only a law of the specified kind and not any action. Thus where a fundamental right is violated by an action, that action shall not be immune from attack. But if the violation is authorised by a law of the kind mentioned in Article 45, no challenge can be maintained. Article 152 defines "disciplined force" as meaning the army, navy or air force, the police force and any other force declared by law to be a disciplined force. Article 152 further defines "disciplinary law" as being a law regulating the discipline of any disciplined force.
34. In the instant case, we find that the impugned action of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner for attempted rape and attempted murder is not authorized by the Navy Ordinance. This is because attempted rape and attempted murder are civil offences as defined in section 4(iii) of the Navy Ordinance and,, as such, before inflicting punishment, the same ought to have been tried by a naval tribunal as per section 78 or by a criminal court pursuant to the concurrent jurisdiction of naval tribunal and criminal court for trial of civil offences under section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and 549 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. The Report of the Board of Inquiry (Annexure 2, Affidavit-in-Opposition) recommended harsh punishment for the Petitioner, which can only be inflicted after the trial process. The National Human Rights Commission through Order No. 7 (Annexure J(1)) disposed of the complaint lodged by the Petitioner by recommending that he should resolve the matter through the courts. The power of compulsory retirement of the Respondents under section 17(1) of the Navy Ordinance should only be exercised in case of misconduct, inefficiency or a reason akin to that (ejusdem generis) as explained in Regulations 0801 and 0807 of the Navy Regulations and not in a case such as the instant case in which the allegations against the Petitioner amount to civil offences, which warrant a trial by a Naval Tribunal as provided in section 78 of the Navy Ordinance or a criminal court under section 107 of the Navy Ordinance and 549 of the Cod of Criminal Procedure 1898. As such, the Petitioner has clearly been illegally removed. In Bangladesh & others vs AKM Zahangir Hossain, 34 DLR (AD) 173, the Hon'ble Appellate Division held that in an appropriate case when a person has been illegally dismissed, removed, discharged, compulsorily retired or reduced in rank, he is entitled to invoke the writ jurisdiction under Article 102.
35. In addition, we are of the view that the instant case has nothing to do with the proper discharge of duties or maintenance of discipline in a disciplined force. It is quite obvious from the Inquiry Report that a simple matter of the lovers' quarrel has been blown out of all proportions. It was a personal matter between a man and a woman which has no connection with either the discharge of duties or the maintenance of discipline in the force. Even if there had been any truth to the allegations of attempted rape and attempted murder, the same also cannot reasonably be considered to be a matter of discipline.
36. We also find convincing the parallel drawn between termination simpliciter without stigma and compulsory retirement without stigma based on the doctrine of pleasure of the president (Article 134 of the Constitution), both of which are immune to challenge. The instant case being one of compulsory retirement with stigma as evident from the second Impugned Order (Annexure A 1) and a host of correspondence/ reports (Annexures G, I(1), I(2), etc.) that followed the first Impugned Order of compulsory retirement is clearly distinguishable and therefore amenable to writ jurisdiction, Article 134 being no bar. In Bangladesh Porjatan Corporation vs Md Ali Hossain, 18 MLR (AD) 265 = 65 DLR (AD) 158 the Court held in paragraph 60 that,
"If the employee is guilty of any offence he may be proceeded with in accordance with the disciplinary procedure available under the rule of the said “কর্মচারী চাকরি প্রবিধানমালা, and if an employee have (has)been found to have been involved in any-offence, as in this case, the said employee may be punished even if (by) imposing the penalty available in the “প্রবিধানমালা”. But under no circumstances, the power of termination simpliciter can be exercised for such offence of the employee." The Court also held in paragraph 43 that, "If the petitioner committed any offence in 2000-2001 as allegedly found by the enquiry committee of the corporation in its report submitted on 31- 12-2001 and then again in 2006, he could be proceeded with and punished under the provisions of the Probidhanmala 1990, but in no case, he could be terminated for commission of such offences."
<u>37. We also find that the Impugned Order of compulsory retirement was not to maintain discipline but to punish the Petitioner in the garb of compulsory retirement without a trial as required by the Navy Ordinance and hence ex facie malafide and a colourable exercise of the Respondent's power under section 17(1) and, as such, the bar in Article 45 and Article 134 to invoking the writ jurisdiction does not apply to the instant case. In Col. Md Hashmat Ali vs Bangladesh 47 DLR (AD) 1 the Hon'ble Appellate Division held that in case of punishment or compulsory retirement that can be construed as punishment, Article 45 does not impose a bar to invoking the writ jurisdiction.</u>
38. As such, for the reasons stated above, the instant writ petition is maintainable and is not barred by Article 45 from challenge under Article 102.
39. Now that we have found the writ petition to be maintainable, we shall review the merits of the case. As stated earlier, it is evident from the Inquiry Report that a simple matter of the lovers' quarrel has been blown out of all proportions and grave injustice has been done to the Petitioner and his family who have been socially ostracised for so many years for crimes he did not commit. He has been presumed to be guilty and punished by an order of compulsory retirement and life-long stigma of attempted rape and murder without being afforded any, far less all the protections of the trial process (under section 78 and section 107 of the Navy Ordinance), including, but not limited to, the right to object to any officer constituting court-martial (section 109), right of trial under the protection of oath by every member of the court-martial (section 110), protection of testimony of witnesses under oath (section 110), protection of rules of evidence (section 114) which includes his right to be presumed innocent until the contrary is proved beyond reasonable doubt, right to cross-examine and test the veracity of the witnesses, right of confirmation, revision and review of the findings of court-martial under Chapter XII of the Navy Ordinance, right of pardons, remissions and suspensions under Chapter XIV of the Navy Ordinance.
40. In view of the above, we do not find any merit in the submissions made on behalf of the Respondent No. 4.
41. We, however, find merit in the submissions of the Learned Advocates for the Petitioner, Mr Akhtar Imam and Ms. Rashna Imam.
42. As such, the Rule is made absolute in part with no order as to costs and the Impugned Memo dated 17-10-2011 (Annexure A) read with the Impugned Memo dated 21-5-2013 [Annexure A(1)] issuing the order of compulsory retirement of the Petitioner is declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and the Petitioner is exonerated from all charges/accusations of attempted rape and murder.
43. In light of the final submission made by Mr Akhtar Imam on behalf of the Petitioner to the effect that the Petitioner after so many years does not want reinstatement in service or back wages or any kind of compensation except to clear his name of such vile allegations like attempted rape and murder, the Rule is discharged to the extent of such prayers in the writ petition.
No order as to costs.
Communicate the judgment and order at once.
End.
