full_judgment:
Md. Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: At the instance of the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 05 of 2009 filed for pre-emption under Mahomedan Law (haq Shufaa), this appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 15-9-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Barguna dismissing the suit. 

2. The short facts in preferring this appeal are: 
The predecessor of the present appellant Nos. 1-6, namely, Alhaj Md. Younus Mia as plaintiff (pre-emptor) filed that suit under Mahomedan Law stating inter alia that, the land appertaining to SA Khatian No. 359 originally belonged to the plaintiff and his full-brother, the defendant No. 2 herein the respondent No. 2. Subsequently, the defendant No. 2 (herein referred to as "seller") sold out 5.32 acres of land appertaining to Plot No. 1320 to the defendant-respondent No. 1 (herein referred to as the "purchaser") without informing the said transfer to the plaintiff. In the suit land, the plaintiff has homestead whereas, the defendant No. 1 is a stranger purchaser in the suit land and the same is used for the communication of the local people, supply of water for cultivation where there remained a haystack as well. On 17-2-2009, after completing court's job, the plaintiff (who being an Advocate by profession) accompanied by his Moharar (clerk) named, Atahar Miah went to the suit plot bearing No. 1320 and found that the defendant No. 1 and other pLi.:,ons are setting up haystack. The plaintiff then asked one, Shahidul Islam in presence of the defendant No. 1 and others about their reason of gathering there, when the defendant No. I apprised him that he purchased the suit land where paddy straws were being stuck. The plaintiff then instantly jumped on the suit property expressing his desire to pre-empt the same and thus performed "Talab-i-Mowasibat" and after obtaining the certified copy of the disputed deed on 26-9-2009, he came to learn about the transfer of the suit land dated 15-7-2008 and as a shafi then filed the suit. 

3. On the contrary, the defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material averments so made in the plaint contending inter alia that, for want of money, the defendant No. 2 at first offered to sell the suit property to the plaintiff but as the plaintiff declined to purchase the suit property and told him to sell it to elsewhere when the defendant No. 1 agreed to purchase the suit property and to that effect, an agreement for sale (বায়নাপত্র) was held with the defendant No. 2 on 19-1-2008. Thereafter, the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 in association with other persons in the locality then made measurement of the suit property and delivered possession to the defendant No. 1. It has further been stated that describing some untrue facts the plaintiff filed the suit as no cause of action as has been narrated in the plaint at all occurred on 17-2-2009 and finally prayed for dismissing the suit. 

4. In order to dispose of the suit, the learned Judge of the trial court framed as many as 5 different issues. To support the case, the plaintiff examined as many as 3(three) witnesses while the defendant No. 1 examined 4(four) witnesses. Apart from that the plaintiff and the defendant No. I also produced several documents which were also marked Exhibits. The learned Joint District Judge however after concluding trial by impugned judgment and decree dismissed the suit holding that, the plaintiff has failed to prove his case and the same is barred by principle of waiver and acquiescence. 

5. It is at that stage, the plaintiff as appellant preferred this appeal. 

6. Mr. Mohammod Hossain, the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant upon taking us to the impugned judgment and all other documents appeared in the paper book, at the very outset submits that, in spite of proving the case by the plaintiff in toto, the learned Joint District Judge has whimsically dismissed the suit which is liable to be set-aside. 

7. To elaborate his submission, the learned counsel then contends that though the defendant No. I tried to assert the facts that on the date of arising cause of action dated 17-2-2009, the defendant No. 1 was not present at the suit plot rather he had been at his office in Munshiganj but that very case could not be inserted in the written statement by way of amendment rather it was rejected by the trial court dated 24-9-2014 yet the learned Judge has illegally taken into account of that very fact and very illegally dismissed the suit so the plaintiff is entitled to get the suit land through pre-emption. 

8. The learned counsel next submits that, though the learned Judge of the trial court while adjudicating the suit found two vital issues bearing issue Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of the plaintiff, so no question can arise not to prove "Talab-i-Mowasi bat" and "Talab-i-Ishhad" when issue No. 2 was framed to the effect that, "বাদীর অগ্রক্রয়ের জন্য উপযুক্ত ব্যক্তি কিনা?" disposed of in favour of the plaintiff and therefore, the trial court has misdirected himself by dismissing the suit. 

9. The learned counsel then by taking us through the plaint, in particular, paragraph Nos. 7 and 8 thereof contends that, the plaintiff upon arriving the suit land on 17-2-2009 and having been informed of its transfer expressed his desire to pre-empt the same by jumping on it while in paragraph No. 8, it has also been stated that the defendant No. 1 refused to register the suit land when he asked for that, having no scope to find that "Talab-i-Ishhad" has not been complied with. 

10. With regard to the definite case of the defendant-respondent that the plaintiff-appellant has failed to prove that he had no knowledge about the disputed sale, the learned counsel then contends that, all the witnesses remained present on the suit plot on 17-2-2009 gave their testimony favouring the plaintiff's case in regard to arising cause of action in line with the assertion made in the plaint having no scope to disbelieve the case of the plaintiff with regard to the date of knowledge. 

11. The learned counsel by referring to the provision of Article 10 of the Limitation Act also contends that, since the suit has been filed on 16-3-2009 that is, within 9(nine) months from the date of disputed sale dated 15-7-2008 so there is no scope to find the suit barred by limitation as has been unfairly found by the learned Judge of the trial court. 

12. Insofar with regard to the alleged agreement for sale (bainapatra) before the disputed sale deed dated 19-1-2008 held between the defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2, the learned counsel submits that, since that bainapatra has not been marked as any Exhibit so the alleged case of measurement (মাপঝোক) to have been done at the instance of the plaintiff does not at all arise yet if any measurement was done then there. would have sketch map to that effect but admittedly nothing to this sort has been produced before the court below and theiefore, the case of the defendant No. 1 to that direction has not been proved at all and therefore, the plaintiff is entitled to the benefit of the presumptive value as provided in illustration (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act. 

13. The learned counsel also contends that, since PW-2 and PW 3 has clearly supported the case of the plaintiff with regard to the date of knowledge about the disputed sale and their testimony could not be shaken by cross-examining them by the defendant, so it also proves that, the suit was filed within time even from the date of knowledge. 

14. With regard to the decision so have been relied by the learned counsel for the defendant-respondent No. 1 reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 332, the learned counsel submits that, the facts so have been discussed and observed in the cited decision is totally distinguishable with the facts and circumstances of the plaintiff's case and then the said decision is totally inapplicable here. 

15. In regard to the decision reported in 13 BLC 606 relied by the respondent No. 1, the learned counsel further contends that the said decision will not be applicable as well, since it has been proved by PW3 vis-à-vis asserted in the plaint in particular in paragraph Nos. 7 and 8 that at the time of "Talab-i-Ishhad", the plaintiff offered the price of the suit value to the purchaser so it proves that on 17-2-2009 both "Talab-i-Mowasibat" and "Talab-i-Ishhad" had rightly been performed by the plaintiff-appellant which has not been discarded by the defendant-respondent. 

16. However, the learned counsel rather placed his reliance to the decision reported in 11 BLC 329 as cited by the learned counsel for the respondent and then submits that it has clearly been held in the said decision that the demands "Talab-i-Mowasibat" and "Talab-i-Ishhad" have to be performed at the same time or in the same sitting which has also been done in the instant case and therefore, the plaintiff is entitled to get the suit land through pre-emption. With these submissions, the learned counsel finally prays for allowing the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

17. On the flipside, Mr. Abdur Rahman, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 1 very robustly opposes the contention taken by the learned counsel for the appellant and submits that, the core point in obtaining any suit land through haq shufaa is guided by the principle of Mahomedan Law and therefore, the principles so laid down therein has to be followed strictly in having any land through haq shuffa (pre-emption). 

18. To supplement the said submission, the learned counsel then referred clause 236 of Mulla's Principles of Mahomedan Law and submits that, based on that provision, two different modes of claim must be performed that is to say, soon after coming to know about selling any property which he/she wants to pre-empt through Mahomedan Law, to jump on the suit land and declare his/her desire to pre-empt the case land which is called "Talab-i-Mowasibat" in other words 'immediate demand' and then the pre-emptor has to offer the price of the suit land either to the buyer or the seller in presence of at least two witnesses which is called "Talab-i-Ishhad", that is, "formal demand" and further submits that, though "Talab-i-Mowasibat" was found to have performed by the plaintiff but from the plaint and the witnesses adduced thereby, it has not been found that "Talab-i-Ishhad" has at all been performed and for that obvious reason, the pre-emption case cannot be sustained. 

19. At this, when we pose a question to the learned counsel for the respondent that the trial court in his entire judgment did not mention those two vital principles under Muslim Law followed in having a land through pre-emption, the learned counsel then retorted that since it is a point of law it can be raised even before the apex court and since this Hon'ble court is an appellate court so within the meaning of section 107 of the Code of Civil Procedure invariably it can certainly adjudicate any point-in-issue as trial court and thereby any factual or legal aspect can be canvassed for its consideration and there is no legal bar to raise such point of law before this Hon'ble court. 

20. The learned counsel by referring to the plaint in particular, paragraph No. 7 thereof then submits that the plaintiff alleged that he came to learn about the disputed sale on 17-2-2009 when he accompanied by his Moharar (Advocate's clerk) appeared in the suit land and then expressed his intention to pre-empt it by jumping on the suit land but the second demand called "Talab-i-Ishhad" has not been performed by the plaintiff by offering price of the suit property either to the purchaser or to the buyer in presence of witnesses by asserting that he had already performed "Talab-i-Mowasibat" so the appeal is liable to be dismissed and the trial court has not erred in law in dismissing the suit. 

21. When we draw attention to the learned counsel that in paragraph No. 8 to the plaint it has been asserted by the plaintiff that  “আমি আমার অফার দাবী আগেই করিয়াছি এবং এখন আবার করিলাম আপনারা আতাহার, সহিদ ও মাহমুব ইহার স্বাক্ষী রহিলেন”, the learned counsel then contends that since that demand has been made as an ordinary manner of title suit when no direct offer as regards to purchase of the suit land has been made to the purchaser so "Talab-i-Ishhad" cannot be said to have performed by the plaintiff and therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled to pre-empt the case land. 

22. Insofar as regards to the limitation in filing the suit, the learned counsel then contends that. since the plaintiff did not claim to have filed the suit as per Article 10 of the Limitation Act, rather he claimed to have filed the suit from the date of knowledge dated 17-2-2009 so the plaintiff is duty bound to prove his such date of knowledge by convincing evidence which he failed rather it has been proved, the plaintiff had earlier knowledge resulting in, the principle of waiver and acquiescence has been operated against the plaintiff and the learned Judge has rightly dismissed the suit on that. 

23. To supplement the above submission, the learned counsel next contends that since it is the definite case of the plaintiff that he accompanied by his clerk who deposed as PW-2 went to the suit property only on 17-2-2009 and in presence of the witnesses, he first came to learn or in other words, became sure about the disputed transfer of the suit property but by giving reference to the evidence of PW-2, the Moharar, the learned counsel then contends that, that PW-2 in his cross-examination clearly asserted that, the plaintiff gathered information about the disputed transfer 7-8 days before by saying that "৭/৮ দিন আগে থেকেই বাদী মামলার জমিতে যাবে মর্মে বলে” for which the date of knowledge as asserted by the plaintiff on 17-2-2009 does not stand rather, it alternatively proves that the plaintiff took active role in measuring the suit land soon after the bainapatra dated 19-1-2008 and the trial court has rightly dismissed the suit finding it barred by principle of waiver and acquiescence. 

24. The learned counsel also contends that, it is rather proved by the defendant No. 1 that on the very date of alleged appearance of the plaintiff in the suit land dated 17-2-2009, he was not present and in support of his such assertion, he also produced a certificate issued by his higher authority by marking it as Exhibit `gha' even without any objection from the plaintiff (page 111 to the paper book) and since that very Exhibit `gha' has been taken into evidence without any objection on the part of the plaintiff, so it also disproves the case of the plaintiff who asserted that the defendant No. 1 remained present on 17-2-2009 and thus the cause of action also does not stand. 

25. In reference to the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant that since the application for amendment brought by the defendant No. 1 asserting that he had been at his office on 17-2-2009 was ultimately rejected by the trial court leaving no scope to mark the certificate as Exhibit `gha', the learned counsel then contends that, since it is the definite case of the defendant that he was not present on that date so there has been no illegality to mark the certificate as Exhibit `gha' in spite of rejecting the application for amendment and therefore, the cause of action in particular, the statement with regard to the presence of the defendant No. 1 in the suit land on 17-2-2009 thus, rendered disproved. 

26. The learned counsel goes on to submit that, soon after the agreement for sale (bainapatra) is done dated 19-1-2008, the plaintiff with the help of other person in the locality got the defendant No. 1 inducted in the suit property on measuring the same and this very fact has vividly been proved by DW-1 to DW-4 who remained present and thereby asserted the written statement and their such testimony has not been shaken on cross-examining them by the plaintiff and there-fore, the case of the defendant No. 1 has been proved that the plaintiff was at first offered to pur-chase the suit land by his full-brother, defendant No. 2 and therefore, the trial court has perfectly found that the suit is barred by principle of waiver and acquiescence and dismissed the suit. 

27. However, in support of his submission, the learned counsel then placed his reliance on the decision reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 332 and 13 BLC 606 and that of an unreported decision passed in First Appeal No. 460 of 2001 dated 24-1-2011 and finally prays for dismissing the appeal. 

28. Be that as it may, we have considered the submission so advanced by the learned counsel for the contending parties at length, perused the impugned judgment and decree and all other documents appeared in the paper book vis-a-vis the provision laid down in clause 236 of Mulla's Principles of Mahomedan Law. 

29. It is an admitted position, while a person claims pre-emption through Mahomedan Law, two basic legal formalities has to be performed by him/her as enshrined in clause 236 of Mahomedan Law though such formalities are absent in section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 where the point of limitation is not that material rather receiving information of sale is vital. For our ready reference, the said provision is thus reproduced below: 
"236. Demands for pre-emption.—No person is entitled to the right of pre-emption unless—
(1) he has declared his intention to the right immediately on receiving information of the sale. This formality is called talab-i-mowasibat (literally, demand of jumping, that is, immediate demand): and unless 
(2) he has with the least practicable delay affirmed the intention, referring expressly to the fact that the talab-i-mowasibat had already been made, and has made a formal demand-
(a) either in the presence of the buyer, or the seller, or on the premises which are the subject of sale, and 
(b) in the presence at least of two witnesses. This formality is called talab-i-ishhad (demand with invocation of witnesses)." 

30. On plain reading of that provision, we find that, when a second demand namely, formal demand by way of "Talab-i-Ishhad" will be made, the pre-emptor has to confirm that he had earlier performed his/her earlier demand/intention called "Talab-i-Mowasibat" and to offer price of the suit land either to the purchaser or seller in presence of at least two witnesses that is sold. But in the instant case, if we go through paragraph No. 7 to the plaint, we find that, the plaintiff expressed his intention to pre-empt the case land in presence of witnesses by jumping on it claiming himself to have performed "Talab-i-Mowasibat". Now, if we peruse paragraph No. 8, we find that as the defendant No. 1 refused to register the sale deed so offered by the plaintiff in presence of the witness, he then filed the suit on obtaining certified copy of the sale deed. Now let us see what has been exactly stated in the relevant part of paragraph No. 8 
"বিরোধীয় ভূমি ছাড়া আমি শাফী (বাদী) ও আমার অন্যান্য লোক জন আদৌ চলাফেরা করিতে পারে না বিধায় কবলা গ্রহিতা ১নং বিবাদীকে (খ) তপছিল বর্ণিত কবলা দলিলের বহায় ৮,০০,০০০ টাকা গ্রহন করিয়া উক্ত কবলা দলিলের অন্তর্ভুক্ত ৫.৩২ একর ভূমির কবলা দলিল আমি শাফীর (বাদী) দাবী মোতাবেক ১নং বিবাদীকে রেজিষ্ট্রি করিয়া দিতে বলিলে কবলা গ্রহিতা ১নং বিবাদী বিগত ইং ১৭-২-০৯ বাংলা ১৪১৫/৫ই ফাল্গুন তারিখে স্বাক্ষী গণের সম্মুখে অস্বীকার করায় আমি শাফী (বাদী) তালাশ অনুসন্ধানে আমতলী এস, আর অফিস হইতে (ক) তপছিল বর্ণিত বিরোধীয় ভূমির কবলা দলিলের সহিমহর নকল ইং ২৬-২-০৯ বাংলা ১৪১৫/১৪ই ফাল্গুন তারিখে হাতে পাইয়া সঠিক ভাবে অবগত হইয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা শাফী (বাদী) আনায়ন করিলেন।"

31. So, from the above, we don't find that on the spot, the plaintiff had offered the price of the suit property to the defendant No. 1 asserting there that he had already performed "Talab-i-Mowasibat". So the submission so placed by the learned counsel for the respondent No. 1 that the plaintiff has not performed "Talab-i-Ishhad" by making formal demand bears ample substance. 

32. Further, we have perused the decision in the Case of Shamsuddin Ahmed @ Tofa Mia and others vs Abdul 1Atif Bhuiyan reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 332: 33 DLR (AD) 359 where it has been fortified the principles laid down in clause 236 of Mahomedan Law in regard to performing the obligation of "Talab-i-Mowasibat" and "Talab-i-Ishhad". The same principle has also been intensified in the decision reported in 13 BLC 606 as well where it was held as under: 
"The plaintiffs have to prove their case independent of the weakness of the defence case. From the deposition of PW-1 it is clear that he did not assert that immediately after he came to know about the sale in question demanded preemption of the land transferred by the kabala in question by jumping and thus talab-e-mowasibat was observed and then he, in presence of the two witnesses by referring to his said immediate demand of preemption requested the seller or the buyer or on the land transferred to accept the kabala money and execute and register the necessary sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs and thus strictly observed the formalities of talab-e-ishaad and therefore, the plaintiffs were entitled to file the suit for preemption. There was no reference of talab-e-mowasibat when he allegedly performed the formalities of talab-e-ishaad. If there was no reference of talab-e-mowasibat at the time of talab-e-ishaad then it would be held that the legal formalities which are condition precedent to exercise the right of preemption under the Mahomedan Law were not observed. Thus, the plaintiffs have failed to observe the legal formalities of talab-e-ishaad and talab-e-mowasibat being the condition precedent to pray for preemption under the Mahomedan Law." 

33. However, relying on the same pro-position of performing talab-i-ishhad and talab-i-mowasibat, this court has also passed a judgment on 9-11-2023 in First Appeal No. 263 of 2020 in line with the decision reported in 19 DLR 759. 

34. Now let us revert to the point of waiver and acquiescence basing on which the learned Judge of the trial court dismissed the suit. It is the case of the plaintiff that he only on 17-2-2009 got to know about the sale of the property and to support the case, he amongst others adduced his clerk, as PW-2 but curiously enough, PW-2 in his cross-examination asserted that, the plaintiff wanted to go to the suit property 7-8 days before which clearly disproved the alleged date of knowledge asserted by the plaintiff rather it conversely proves that, the plaintiff had earlier knowledge of the disputed sale and he got the suit land measured through a Surveyor and others after the bainapatra dated 19-1-2008 and handed over possession of the suit land to the defendant No. 1. 

35. It is admitted position that, the defendant No. 2 and the plaintiff are two full-brothers and it has also been found from the cross-examination of PW-2 that, it takes only 20 minutes to go to the suit property from the house of the plaintiff which is only kilometer away from his house. So it is quite impractical to assume that the plaintiff had no knowledge about the disputed transfer by his full-brother, defendant No. 2 to defendant No. 1. Furthermore, apart from defendant No. 1 who deposed as DW-1 all other witnesses so adduced by the defendants as DW-2 to DW-4 asserted that soon after the agreement for sale (bainapatra) dated 19-1-2008, the plaintiff by remaining present along with Surveyor and others upon making measurement of the suit land inducted defendant No. I into possession and those witnesses have been extensively cross-examined by the plaintiff but no deviation can be made from their such assertion rather what has been asserted by the defendant No. 1 in his written statement to the effect that, ""ইতিমধ্যে অন্য মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ ও ২নং কেবলা দাতা"। বিবাদী ১৪১ সালে ফাল্ভূমিগুন ৫-১১ তারিখ পর্যন্ত মোকদ্দমার লড়াইয়ে অবস্থানে অবস্থান সার্ভেয়ার আবদুস সোবহান আকন, স্থানীয় জামাল খাও মোশারেফ হোসেন হাং এর ঘাতকদের মাধ্যমে জমিজমা ভাগ বন্টন ক্রমে সীমানা নির্ধারণ করিয়া অত্র উত্তরদায়ক ১নং কবলা গ্রহীতা বরাবরে হস্তান্তরিত ৫.৩২ একর ভূমিতে পৃথক সীমানা পিলার দ্বারা দখল বুঝাইয়া দেন। তাহাতে বাদী, ১/২ নং বিবাদী ও অপর এক কবলা দারের ৩.০৮% একর ভূমি পৃথক পৃথক ভাবে বুঝিয়া নিয়া একে অপরের দখল স্বীকার করিয়া দেন। has rather been corroborated by all the person named therein the above assertion as DWs. Though it is the assertion of the learned counsel for the appellants that since the amendment of the defendant No. 1 with regard to his presence in his office on 17-2-2009 has been rejected on 24-9-2014 so his certificate marked as Exhibit-`gha' cannot be taken into account. But such submission cannot sustain as the defendant No. 1 in paragraph No. 14 to his written statement clearly denied the cause of action as alleged by the plaintiff. So, mere rejecting the amendment application does not ipso facto debar the defendant to produce and mark a document in regard to his absence on the date of arising cause of action when admittedly the said Exhibit-'gha' was marked even without any objection from the plaintiff side. 

36. At the fag-end of the hearing, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that, under illustrations (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act, the presumption of alleged participation of the plaintiff in measuring the suit land and to hand over possession of the same in favour of the defendant No. 1 goes against the plaintiff as no bainapatra dated 19-1-2008 let alone any sketch map thereof has been produced. But from the written statement filed by the defendant No. 1, we don't find that the defendant No. 1 ever claimed to execute any bainapatra in black and white let alone drawn any sketch map rather what he stated in the written statement that "অত্র মোকদ্দমার ২নং কবলা দাতা বিবাদী ও ১নং কবলা গ্রহীতা বিবাদী ১৯-১-২০০৮ তারিখ চুক্তিবদ্ধ হন ". So, from the above assertion, the provision of the Evidence Act as relied upon by the learned counsel clearly falls through. 

37. Insofar as regards to the application of Article 10 of the Limitation Act in filing the suit in time as canvassed by the learned counsel for the appellant, we are of the view that, the plaintiff has not asserted so in his plaint, rather the plaintiff claimed to have filed the suit from the date of knowledge dated 17-2-2009 as described in paragraph Nos. 7-8 and asserted to have filed the suit within 29 days of accruing date of knowledge (suit filed on 16-3-2009) leaving it to the plaintiff to prove that very date of knowledge by convincing evidence. 

38. However, it has been observed hereinabove from the testimony of PW-2 who clearly asserted in reply to his cross-examination that the plaintiff had knowledge earlier about the disputed transfer as he (plaintiff) disclosed him to go to the suit property 7-8 days ago. So with that assertion, the alleged date of knowledge of the plaintiff about the disputed sale has clearly shifted having no scope to bank-upon Article 10 of the Limitation Act now and therefore, the cause of action in filing the suit stands disproved. 

39. All in all, given the above facts and circumstances vis-a-vis the discussion and observation made hereinabove, we don't find any merit in the appeal that warrants any interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

40. As a result, we don't find any illegality in the impugned judgment and decree which is liable to be sustained. 

41. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed however without any order as to costs. 

Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower court records be transmitted to the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Barguna forthwith. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13.02.2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.766, 803, 1242 and 1478 all of 2012).
full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub, J: 1. Since common question of law and similar facts are involved in all those 4(four) civil appeals, as such, those have been heard together and are being disposed of by this single judgment. 

2. These civil appeals by leave are directed against the judgment and order dated 13.02.2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.766, 803, 1242 and 1478 all of 2012 making the Rule absolute with necessary directions. 

3. Facts, in connection with Civil Appeal No.171 of 2015 arising out of Writ Petition No.766 of 2012, in brief, are that pursuant to long term Settlement Case No.1/92-93 the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong executed a registered deed dated 21.03.1994 in favour of the respondent-writ petitioner for 99 years covering an area of 19.29 acres corresponding to B.S. Dag No.1, Mouja-Majherchar, Police Station-Anwara, District-Chittagong. Accordingly, Mutation Case No.1099/2009-2010 was opened in the name of the writ-petitioner, who, upon paying land development tax, had been enjoying possession thereof without any objection from any quarter whatsoever. 

4. Meanwhile, Land Acquisition Case No.1/2010-2011 was initiated by the authority concerned to acquire 144.05 acres of land of Rangadia Mouja and 451.31 acres of land situated under Majherchar Mouja including the land of the writ-petitioner with publication of notice under Section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982(in short, the Ordinance, 1982). The writ-petitioner duly raised objection thereto vide letter dated 19.08.2010. In this regard, their categorical assertion is that neither they were heard nor their objection was disposed of. 

5. Further assertion of the writ-petitioner is that when the proposal with concise report dated 02.11.2011 was placed before the Hon’ble Prime Minister of the Republic for final approval, in view of Section 5(1) of the Ordinance, 1982, it was sent back to the Ministry concerned on 14.11.2010 with the following remarks: "এমতাবস্থায়, বর্ণিত সমস্যা/ত্রুটিসমূহ আপনোদনপূর্বক সুস্পষ্ট মতামতসহ পুনরায় সার-সংক্ষেপ প্রেরণের জন্য ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়কে অনুরোধ করা যেতে পারে।” 

6. However, the emphatic claim of the respondent-writ petitioner is that the Ministry of Land never submitted any concise report or fresh summary in compliance of the said direction. Rather, without obtaining approval of the Prime Minister, the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Land, vide the impugned Memo bearing No. ভূঃমঃ/ অধিশাখা-১১/অধিঃ/চট্ট-১২৮/-২১০-২৯৬ dated 23.11.2010, gave final approval on behalf of the appellant-respondent government to acquire 07.60 acres of private land and to transfer 587.60 acres of “khas” land under clause 7 of the Land Acquisition Manual, 1997 for construction of coal based power plant jetty and cold storage yard with direction upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong (now, Chattogram) to take necessary steps in due compliance of law. 

7. Being aggrieved thereby led to filing the writ petition before the High Court Division under Article 102 of Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, whereupon a Rule Nisi was issued. 

8. Short facts in relation to Civil Appeal No.172 of 2015 arising out of Writ Petition No. 803 of 2012 are that the appellant-respondent Government, vide registered lease deed No.1817 of 1961, leased out 109.71 acres of land under R.S. Dag Nos.241/3C,241/2C,241/4C,241/9C,241/7A,241/6A,241/5A,241/10A corresponding to B.S. Khatian No.154, B.S. Dag Nos.1001-1025, 1086-1096, 1100-1101, 1104-1117, 1120-1121, 1126-1128, 1136-1139, Mouja-Rangadia, Police Station-Kornophully, District-Chittagong and 75 acres of land under R.S. Dag No.1/A corresponding to B.S. Khatian No.3, B.S. Dag No.1, Mouja-Majherchar, Police Station-Kornophully, District-Chittagong, in total 184.71 acres of land in favour of the respondent-writ petitioner for 25 (twenty five) years, with possession thereof. Said lease period was subsequently renewed for another 25 (twenty five) years vide registered Renewal Deed No.1769 dated 29.03.2009. 

9. While the respondent-writ petitioner was enjoying possession of the said properties upon paying due land development tax as was required under the law, notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 was issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong in connection with L.A. Case No. 1/2010-2011. The respondent-writ petitioner raised objection thereto on 09.08.2010 and again, on 22.08.2010 respectively; those were duly received by the authority concerned. 

10. It is also the categorical assertion of the respondent-writ petitioner that despite the fact that the appellant-writ respondent No.2 was not empowered to reject the objection of the writ petitioner he, upon rejecting the said objection, sent a report to the Ministry of Land for approval. On receipt thereof, said Ministry prepared a summary for the Hon’ble Prime Minister for approval vide Memo No. ভূঃমঃ/ অধিশাখা-১১/অধিঃ/চট্ট-১২৮/-২১০-২৪০ dated 02.11.2010, but without including the objection being raised by the respondent-writ petitioner. The then Prime Minister of the Republic, not being satisfied with the said concise report, sent it back to the Ministry concerned vide note dated 14.11.2010 with direction to submit a new summary with necessary clarification. But without sending report afresh, the Ministry of Land issued the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010. 

11. On the contention that the initiation and continuation of the said L.A. proceeding was illegal and hence, it was liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect, the respondent-writ petitioner filed writ petition before the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution. Having found prima-facie substance, a Rule Nisi was issued by the said Division.

12. Short facts in connection with Civil Appeal No.173 of 2015 arising out of Writ Petition No.1242 of 2012, are that writ-respondent No.1, i.e. Chittagong Port Authority leased out 264 acres of land of B.S. Plot No.101, 1(p), 114(p), Mouja-Majherchar, P.S.-Karnaphuli (Bandar), Upzilla-Anwara, District-Chittagong in favour of the respondent-writ petitioner on execution of a lease agreement dated 04.05.2006 for the purpose of Container Freight Station (CFS), Inland Container Depot (ICD), Supply Based Station (SBS), port based and also, port and shipping related industries. While the writ petitioner was enjoying possession thereof on payment of Tk.47 crores as rent on account of the lease agreement, respective notices were issued upon it by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 in connection with L.A. Case No.1/2010-2011 for acquisition of the properties including the properties of the writ petitioner. 

13. Challenging the proceedings of the said L.A. Case, the respondent-writ petitioner instituted Other Suit No.130 of 2011 before the Court of First Joint District Judge, Chittagong. During pendency of the said suit, the Ministry of Land issued the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 with direction upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to transfer the case property of the writ petitioner in favour of the requiring body, treating the properties as “khas” land. In the given context, allowing the prayer of the respondent-writ petitioner, the concerned Court below dismissed the suit for non-prosecution vide order dated 03.04.2012. 

14. At the same, challenging the impugned memo dated 23.11.2010, issued by the Ministry of Land, the writ petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1242 of 2012 before the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution on the contention that the case property belonged to Chittagong Port Authority and that those were not acquired by the authority concerned in connection with L.A. Case No.1 of 2010-2011.As such, giving direction upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to transfer the case land in favour of the requiring body under Article 7 of the Land Acquisition Manual, 1997 was unlawful. 

15. The writ petitioner also relied upon the Note dated 14.11.2010, claiming to have been signed by the then Hon’ble Prime Minister of the Republic in order to challenge the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 issued by the Ministry concerned. 

16. Having found prima-facie substance a Rule Nisi was issued. 

17. Brief facts in connection with Civil Appeal No.174 of 2015 arising out of Writ Petition No.1478 of 2012, are that the respondent-writ petitioner is the owner of 0.66 acre of land in connection with B.S. Plot No.1144, 0.18 acre of B.S. Plot No.1145, 0.47 acre of B.S. Plot No.1146, 0.77 acre of B.S. Plot No.1147, 1.70 acre of B.S. Plot No.1148, 3.12 acres of B.S. Plot Nos.1149, 1152 and 1153, B.S. Khatian No.33, corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.12, R.S. Plot No.56, P.S. Plot No.429, J.L. No. P.S. 5, B.S. 31 of Rangadia Mouja, Union-Boyrag, Upozilla-Anwara, at present-Karnafuly, District-Chittagong. 

18. While the respondent-writ petitioner was enjoying possession thereof on payment of land development tax regularly in due compliance of law, a notice was issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 for acquisition of properties including the properties of the writ petitioner in connection with L.A. Case No.1 of 2010-2011. Pursuant to the said notice, the writ petitioner duly raised objection, which was ultimately rejected by the authority concerned. Accordingly, the Ministry of Land prepared a concise report dated 02.11.2010 for placing the same before the then Hon’ble Prime Minister for her approval. Relying upon the Note dated 14.11.2010 their further claim was that pursuant thereto the then Hon’ble Prime Minister gave direction upon the Ministry concerned to submit concise report afresh, which was not complied with. 

19. At this juncture, challenging the proceeding of L.A. Case No.1 of 2010-2011 the respondent-writ petitioner as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No.130 of 2011 before the Court of First Joint District Judge, Chittagong. Subsequently, the writ-petitioner having come to learn as to issuance of notice under Section 6 of the Ordinance vide Memo dated 31.01.2012 for taking possession of the case land, made a prayer before the concerned court below to dismiss the suit for non-prosecution, which was duly allowed vide order dated 03.04.2012. 

20. In the given facts and circumstances, the respondent-writ petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1478 of 2012 before the High Court Division upon the contention that without execution of any agreement with the requiring body, the L.A. proceeding was without jurisdiction. Their further claim was that the then Hon’ble Prime Minister never approved acquisition of the case land in connection with the said L.A. Case. Hence, the impugned proceeding was liable to be declared unlawful. 

21. Having found prima-facie substance a Rule Nisi was accordingly issued. 

22. All those Rules Nisi, except the Rule in connection with Writ Petition No.1478 of 2012, were contested by the appellant-writ respondent, Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong by filing separate sets of affidavits-in-opposition, stating, inter-alia, that the whole process of L.A. Case No. 1 of 2010-2011 was initiated in due compliance of law upon providing opportunities to the respective respondents-writ petitioners of being heard. Also, upon taking due approval of the Government under Section 5(1) of the Ordinance, 1982, the impugned Memo dated 23.10.2010 was issued with a direction upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to take necessary steps in due compliance of law. 

23. Upon hearing the respective contending parties, the High Court Division, vide judgment and order dated 13.02.2014, disposed of all the 4(four) writ petitions making the Rules absolute upon declaring the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 to have been issued without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect, with the following observations and findings: 
“Therefore, if a land is vested in the Government, the said land ipso facto does not become the property of a statutory corporation or a local authority, unless the Government transfers the said land to the said statutory corporation such as PDB and PDB has also to acquire such land in compliance of provision of section 3 of the said Order of 1972. Therefore, in our view, since PDB ipso facto shall not become owner of the land when it vests in the Government, and since PDB is though a Governmental authority in nature, but is not Government unto itself, further action on behalf of the Government is required to transfer the land to PDB....... Therefore, PDB shall not become owner of the land unless the same is transferred to PDB by Government under section 15(2) of the said Ordinance and for this reason section 15(1) of the said Ordinance has to be complied with by way of executing a prior agreement between PDB and the Government. 

24. Apart from this, another aspect that calls for consideration is that the Ministry of Land submitted a summary dated 02.11.2010 before the Hon'ble Prime Minister of the Republic. But the Hon'ble Prime Minister vide note dated 14.11.2010 directed the Ministry of Republic to submit a new summary afresh. 

25. We do not find anything which shows the Ministry of Land to comply with the direction of the Prime Minister made in note dated 14.11.2010. The contesting respondent stated in respect of the said note dated 14.11.2010 that it is unaware of any omission of the Government in this respect. The Ministry of Land did not file any affidavit-in-opposition. Therefore, the said note dated 14.11.2010 leads us to irresistible conclusion that the Prime Minister never had the opportunity to approve the said acquisition of land in the said L/A case. 

26. It is also pertinent to mention that Memo No. তৃঃমাঃ/শা-৫/১ আঃ (খুঃ)-15/2002/378(64) dated 01.09.2002 issued by the Ministry of Land itself clarifies that if the proposed acquisition exceeds 50 standard bighas, the approval of the Prime Minister shall be required. 

27. Therefore, we are of the view that even if only 7.86 acres of land has been directed to be acquired by the Ministry of Land, but since the land required for the whole project of PDB exceeds 50 standard bighas of land, the approval of the Hon'ble Prime Minister is required and in the cases in hand, we cannot lose sight of the fact that the Prime Minister had never had the opportunity to ponder over such approval as Ministry of Land did never submit a new summary as directed by Hon'ble Prime Minister vide note dated 14.11.2010. The action of Ministry of Land in issuing the said memo dated 23.11.2010 directing the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to acquire the said 7.86 acres of land and to transfer rest of the land to the requiring body instead of complying with the direction of Hon'ble Prime Minister to submit fresh summary is an outright deviation from direction of Hon'ble Prime Minister which is absolutely unconstitutional being flagrant violation of authority of the Hon'ble Prime Minister under Article 55(2) of the Constitution. 

28. The action of the Ministry of Land in the said impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 is absolutely malafide and such malafide action goes to the root of the jurisdiction and hence the same is without jurisdiction. Further, the whole L/A proceeding being a nullity, the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 issued and all further actions pursuant to the said L/A proceeding is also a nullity” 

29. Being aggrieved, the writ-respondent No.1, the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, as petitioner, preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal bearing Nos.1869, 1870, 1871, and 1872 all of 2014 before this Division under Article 103 of the Constitution. 

30. After hearing the parties concerned, leave was granted by this Division in all the civil petitions vide order dated 26.02.2015 on 4(four) counts. However, the following, being relevant, is quoted below:
II. Because, the High Court Division committed an error in relying upon an alleged letter dated 08.11.2010 showing further clarification which was allegedly sought from the office of the Prime Minister to the Ministry of Land without asking the Government to produce the relevant file; however, had the original file been called for, it would have had appeared that there was no existence of any alleged letter which was produced by the writ petitioner and it was nothing but a concocted one; as such, interference by this Division is called for Consequent thereto instant civil appeals arose. 

31. Mr. Md. Assaduzzaman, the learned Attorney General appearing with Mr. Annek R. Hoque, the learned Additional Attorney General for the appellant categorically submits that in order to seek equitable relief under Article 102 of the Constitution, the foremost important principle which an aggrieved person is required to follow is to invoke writ jurisdiction with clean hand. If any question arises on that count, it shall be considered as a disentitling factor to grant relief, as prayed for. 

32. In the instant case, he submits, the cardinal assertions of the respondents-writ petitioners, among others, are that pursuant to Note no.4 dated 14.11.2010, necessary direction was given by the then Hon’ble Prime Minister of the Republic upon the Ministry of Land to furnish a fresh concise report in view of incomplete information as to disposal of objections being raised by the parties concerned, but that writ-respondent no.1 never sent fresh concise report. Ultimately, without taking approval of the then Hon’ble Prime Minister, the appellant-writ respondent no.1, vide the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010, directed writ-respondent no.2 to take necessary steps in connection with the properties in question in due compliance of law. 

33. Said assertion of the respondents-writ petitioners, he submits, are incorrect, for, Note no.4 containing the signature of the then Hon’ble Prime Minister seeking further clarification from the concerned Ministry, as reproduced and quoted in the writ petitions, are non-existent; hence, those are the product of concoction/forgery. 

34. In this regard, he also goes to argue that had the original file been called for, it would have appeared before the High Court Division that there was no existence of the alleged letter/note dated 08.11.2010 in the respective record. The High Court Division, however, basing on the said non-existent letter, categorically found that the Ministry of Land never sent any report, as required by the then Hon’ble Prime Minister and suppressing the said fact, had issued the impugned memo dated 23.11.2010. Ultimately, the respective Rules were made absolute terming the action of the Ministry concerned mala fide with declaration that the whole process of L.A. Case No.1 of 2010-2011 is without jurisdiction. 

35. In the given facts and circumstances, he submits, the impugned judgment and order 13.02.2014 passed by the High Court Division in all the 4 (four) writ petitions is liable to be knocked down for being based on forged documents. 

36. No one appears on behalf of the respondents-writ petitioners to contest the instant appeals. 

37. The obligations of a litigant while approaching the Court for redressal of his grievances must be with “clean hands”. Courts have, over the centuries, frowned upon litigants who, with intent to deceive and mislead the Courts, initiated proceeding without full disclosure of facts and came to the Courts with “unclean hands”. Courts have held that such litigants are neither entitled to be heard on merit nor are entitled to any relief, interim or final: Kishore Samrite -Vs- State of U.P. (2013) 2 SCC 398. 

38. In the instant case, the respondents-writ petitioners, while challenging the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010, issued by the Ministry of Land under Section 5(1) of the Ordinance, 1982, have admittedly based their foundation on the note dated 14.11.2010, as quoted/reproduced in the respective writ petitions, on the contention that the then Hon’ble Prime Minister, vide the said note dated 14.11.2010, directed the Ministry concerned to submit a summary afresh. However, the said Ministry, without complying said direction, i.e. without sending the said summary afresh, had approved the acquisition process with direction upon the concerned Deputy Commissioner to take steps for transferring the properties in question to the requiring body. 

39. It appears from record that the Ministry of Land did not enter appearance in the respective writ petitions to contest the Rules Nisi. The Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, however, contested the Rules by filing separate sets of affidavit-in-opposition stating, interalia, that “the concise report dated 02.11.2010 of the Ministry of Land, as quoted in paragraph-23, is matter of record (paragraph 18 of affidavit-in-opposition dated 15.04.2012). The contents of note of Prime Minister dated 14.11.2010 directing the Ministry of Land by the Prime Minister to submit further concise report, as quoted in paragraph No.24 of the writ petition, are also matter of records. The Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong merely acted as per final orders and instructions of Government based on the impugned Memo No. ভূঃমঃ/অধিশাখা-১১/অধিঃচট্ট ১২৮/২০১০-২৯৬ dated 23.11.2010 issued by the Ministry of Land and the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong is unaware of any act of omission committed by Ministry of Land in issuing the said impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010, the contents of which are matters of record (paragraph No.20 of affidavit-in-opposition dated 15.04.2012 and Annexure-5 of the affidavit-in-opposition dated 15.04.2012).” 

40. Taking cognizance of Note no.4 dated 14.11.2010 and also, of the assertions of the respondents-writ petitioners that the Ministry concerned approved the acquisition process vide Memo dated 23.11.2010 without sending summary afresh in compliance of the direction of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the High Court Division categorically found the action of the said Ministry to be malafide and hence, without jurisdiction. 

41. During the course of hearing of the instant Civil Appeals, the categorical contention of the appellant-writ respondent has been that in the original file of the concerned Ministry, there is no existence of the alleged letter/note dated 14.11.2010, which was reproduced/quoted in the respective writ petitions and that respondents-writ petitioners have obtained the relief in the High Court Division exercising fraud upon the Court; hence, the impugned judgment and order dated 13.02.2014 passed by the High Court Division is liable to be struck down. 

42. This Division, however, finds substance to the said contention in view of the fact that in para 23 of Writ Petition No.766 of 2012, the respondent-writ petitioner has quoted/reproduced the summary dated 02.11.2010 prepared for the then Hon’ble Prime Minister of the Republic, a confidential document, without disclosing as to how they managed to obtain the same and for using them in a court proceeding without being duly authorised, is a punishable offence under the Official Secret Act, 1923. 

43. It is surprising to note that during the course of hearing of the Rules before the High Court Division, neither the Ministry of Land as writ respondent No.1 entered appearance to contest the Rules to clarify the veracity of the said contents nor the appellant-writ respondent No.2 raised any objection whatsoever to the same. Rather, in their affidavits-in-opposition, they discharged their duties negligently by merely stating that the summary note dated 08.11.2010, as reproduced in para24 of Writ Petition No.766 of 2012, are matters of record. 

44. In the given facts and circumstances, the said stand of the appellant-writ respondent No.2 is unfortunate, unacceptable and hence, strongly deprecated. 

45. However, fact remains, after granting leave by this Division vide order dated 26.02.2015, in particular on ground No. II, corresponding to Note no.4 dated 14.11.2010, the respondent-writ petitioners, in their concise statements, could not controvert the assertion of the appellant-writ respondent No.1 that there is no existence of the alleged note/letter dated 08.11.2010, which was reproduced by the respondents-writ petitioners. 

46. In the given facts and circumstances, the contents of the summary dated 08.11.2010, as reproduced in the respective writ petitions, showing endorsement of the signature of the then Hon’ble Prime Minister dated 14.11.2010, is found to be fictitious and a non-existent letter. 

47. In Lazarus Estate Ltd. Vs. Beasley, (1956) 1 QB 702 PP. 712 and 713, Lord Denning observed: “No judgment of a Court, no order of a Minister can be allowed to stand if it has been obtained by fraud. Fraud unravels everything.” 

48. In the same judgment, Lord Parker L.J. observed that: “Fraud vitiates all transactions known to the law of however high a degree of solemnity.” 

49. The High Court Division, while declaring the entire proceedings of L.A. Case No.1/2010-2011 including the impugned Memo dated 23.11.2010 issued by the Ministry of Land as being unlawful, malafide and without jurisdiction, took cognizance of the said fictitious and non-existent note/concise report dated 08.11.2010. Resultantly, the entire judgment and order dated 13.02.2014 by the High Court Division is vitiated with fraud and the same is, accordingly, struck down. 

50. In the result, all the civil appeals bearing Nos.171-174 of 2015 are hereby allowed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder, J: On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule, at the instance of the defendant-petitioner, was issued calling the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the Order No. 1 dated 30-8-2022 passed by the learned District Judge, Chattogram allowing the application for stay in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 and thereby staying the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021, should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The plaintiffs' case, in brief, is that RS Plot No. 1123 measuring 19 decimals of land belonged to one Har Kumar Mohajon and during the operation of RS record-of-right, 2 decimals out of the said 19 decimals was acquired for the Railway; Har Kumar Mohajon while enjoying and possessing the land, transferred it in favour of Abul Kalam and Abu] Hasim, the predecessors of the plaintiffs, vide registered deed being No. 5894 dated 12-11-1955 and accordingly, RS record-of-right was prepared in their names; subsequently, Abul Kalam while enjoying and possessing over 8.5 decimals died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and in the same way, Abul Hasim died leaving plaintiff Nos. 5-9; RS Plot No. 1119 measuring 19 decimals of land also belonged to Har Kumar Mohajon and while he was enjoying and possessing the same, transferred it in favour of Basir Ullah Sukani, the father of Abul Kalam and Abul Hasim, the predecessors of the plaintiffs, vide registered deed being No. 112 dated 11-1-1949; subsequently, the said Basir Ullah died leaving 3 sons, namely Abul Kalam, Abul Hasim and Abu Jafor and 3 daughters, namely-Rehana, Shaheda and Tahera Begum and by virtue of amicable partition, Abul Kalam and Abul Hasim obtained the land amounting to 19 decimals in their share; subsequently, Abul Kalam while enjoying and possessing the land died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and Abul Hasim died leaving plaintiff Nos. 5-9; on 22-4-2021, the defendant Nos. 8-11 claimed the suit land denying the title of the plaintiffs claiming the same by virtue of registered deeds being Nos. 2467 and 4744 dated 11-5-1966 and 19-10-1966 executed by Basir Ullah, the predecessor of the plaintiff in favour of one Layla Begum, and subsequent transfer by the said Layla Begum in favour of the defendant Nos. 8-11, vide registered deed No. 407 dated 15-4-1996 and hence, the plaintiffs filed the instant case/suit. 

3. The case of the defendant Nos. 8-11 is that they are the genuine owner of the suit land and the plaintiffs and other defendants are claiming the suit land by creating fake mutation in their names and for this reason, the suit/ application for injunction may be dismissed/ rejected for ends of justice. 

4. During pendency of the suit, the defendant Nos. 8-11 filed an application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 before the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021 against the plaintiffs and others not to interfere with the petitioners' peaceful possession and enjoyment over the land-in-question stating, inter alia, that the defendants have already been possessing over the disputed land and accordingly sought temporary injunction over the disputed land so that the miscreants would not dispossess the defendants. 

5. It is stated that after hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the learned trial Judge granted status quo over the land-in-question, vide order No. dated 20-6-2022 in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2022. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Suit No. 1141 of 2022, the plaintiff-appellants preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 before the learned District Judge, Chattogram, who after hearing the appelants, allowed the application for stay in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 by staying the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021, vide order dated 30-8-2022. 

7. As against the aforesaid order the defendant petitioner has filed this civil revision and obtained this Rule along with an order of status quo in respect of possession and position of the suit land. 

8. At the very outset, Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that since the plaintiff by dint of some registered deed claimed the suit land and that he is in possession over the suit land, the learned trial Judge considering all the aspects of the matter rightly passed an order directing both the parties to maintain status quo in respect of position and possession of the suit land and also directing both the parties not to transfer the suit land to anybody else until disposal of the suit. 

9. He next submits that the learned District Judge, Chattogram committed an error of law staying the order of ad-interim temporary injunction dated 20-6-2022 over the land-in-question passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakundu, Chattogram without applying a judicial mind, which appears to have committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case and hence, the order dated 30-8-2022 passed by the learned District Judge, Chattogram in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 is liable to be set-aside. 

10. He then submits that the learned District Judge, Chattogram while staying the order of ad-interim temporary injunction dated 20-6-2022 over the land-in-question failed to appreciate that the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram passed the order of ad-interim temporary injunction upon finding the prima facie title and exclusive possession of the defendant Nos. 8-11 along with rightly finding out the balance of inconvenience in favour of them but he learned District Judge has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

11. He candidly submits that the learned District Judge, Chattogram most illegally passed the non-speaking and mute order and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

12. He additionally submits that the learned District Judge committed serious error of law, and thus stayed the order of the trial Court and, as such, the impugned order lacks in legal sanctity and propriety, hence the learned District Judge has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

13. He strenuously submits that the learned trial Judge on consideration of materials on record rightly granted ad-interim injunction, but the learned Judge of the appellate Court most illegally stayed the order of ad-interim injunction and committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

14. He vigorously submits that the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Sadar, Chattogram after hearing the parties by his order No. 15 dated 20-6-2022, considering the prima facie case, balance of convenience and inconvenience and considering the irreparable loss and injury granted ad-interim temporary injunction in respect of tile and possession of the land-in-question but the order has been stayed by the learned District Judge without assigning any cogent reason and hence, the impugned order may be set-aside. 

15. He categorically submits that the learned District Judge, Chattogram failed to appreciate that the categorical case of the defendant Nos. 8-11 claiming one Layla Begum obtained the suit land measuring 29 decimals by virtue of registered deeds being Nos. 2467 and 4744 dated 11-5-1966 and 19-10-1966 from Basir Ullah, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and accordingly, BS record-of-right was prepared in her name and subsequently, the said Layla Begum transferred the land to the defendant Nos. 8-11, vide registered deed No. 407 dated 15-4-1996 who accordingly, mutated their names and have been possessing the land-in-question by paying taxes/rents but the learned District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

16. He lastly submits that the learned District Judge, Chattogram committed serious illegality in staying the order of the trial Court over the suit land without serving any notice gravely prejudicing the defendant Nos. 8-11 putting them in risk of dispossession from the land-in-question by the plaintiffs and hence the learned District Judge have committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in the case. 

17. No one appears on behalf of the opposite-parties to oppose the Rule. 

18. We have gone through the revisional application and perused the materials annexed thereto. 

19. We have also heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, at length and considered his submissions to the best of my wit and wisdom. 

20. It appears from the record that the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of title before the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge Sitakunda, Chattogram stating inter alia that RS Plot No. 1123 measuring 19 decimals of land belonged to one Har Kumar Mohajon and during the operation of RS record-of-right, 2 decimals out of the said 19 decimals was acquired for the Railway; Har Kumar Mohajon while enjoying and possessing the land, transferred it in favour of Abul Kalam and Abul Hasim, the predecessors of the plaintiffs, vide registered deed being No. 5894 dated 12-11-1955 and accordingly, RS record-of-right was prepared in their names; subsequently, Abu] Kalam while enjoying and possessing over 8.5 decimals died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and in the same way, Abul Hasim died leaving plaintiff Nos. 5-9; RS Plot No. 1119 measuring 19 decimals of land also belonged to Har Kumar Mohajon and while he was enjoying and possessing the same, transferred it in favour of Basir Ullah Sukani, the father of Abul Kalam and Abul Hasim, the predecessors of the plaintiffs, vide registered deed being No. 112 dated 11-1-1949; subsequently, the said Basir Ullah died leaving 3 sons, namely Abu] Kalam, Abul Hasim and Abu Jafor and 3 daughters, namely-Rehana, Shaheda and Tahera Begum and by virtue of amicable partition, Abul Kalam and Abul Hasim obtained the land amounting to 19 decimals in their share; subsequently, Abul Kalam while enjoying and possessing the land died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and Abu] Hasim died leaving plaintiff Nos. 5-9; on 22-4-2021, the defendant Nos. 8-11 claimed the suit land denying the title of the plaintiffs claiming the same by virtue of registered deeds being Nos. 2467 and 4744 dated 11-5-1966 and 19-10-1966 executed by Basir Ullah, the predecessor of the plaintiff in favour of one Layla Begum, and subsequent transfer by the said Layla Begum in favour of the defendant Nos. 8-11, vide registered deed No. 407 dated 15-4-1996. 

21. The case of the defendant Nos. 8-11 is that they are the genuine owner of the suit land and the plaintiffs and other defendants are claiming the suit land by creating fake mutation in their names and for this reason, the suit/application for injunction may be dismissed/rejected for ends of justice. 

22. During pendency of the suit, the defendant Nos. 8-11 filed an application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 before the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021 against the plaintiffs and others not to interfere with the petitioners' peaceful possession and enjoyment over the land-in-question stating, inter alia, that the defendants have already been possessing over the disputed land and accordingly sought temporary injunction over the disputed land so that the miscreants would not dispossess the defendants. 

23. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the learned trial Judge granted status quo over the land-in-question, vide order No. dated 20-6-2022 in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2022. 

24. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Suit No. 1141 of 2022, the plaintiff-appellants preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 before the learned District Judge, Chattogram, who after hearing the appellants, allowed the application for stay in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 by staying the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021, vide order dated 30-8-2022. 

25. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order, the defendant petitioner filed this revisional application before this court and obtained this Rule along with an order of status quo directing both the parties to maintain status quo in respect of position and possession of the suit land in question. 

26. On going through the impugned order and other materials on record, it appears that both the plaintiffs and the defendants are claiming title and possession over the suit land in question by dint of registered deeds. From the claim and counter-claim of the parties, the subject matter of the suit has become a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided by the learned trial Judge without taking evidence from the witnesses of the respective parties. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances the learned trial Judge upon hearing the parties rightly directed both the parties to maintain status quo in respect of position and possession of the suit land and not to sell the suit property to anybody else until the suit is disposed of on merit. However the plaintiffs and others being aggrieved by the same preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 along with an application for stay of the order of status quo passed by the learned trial Judge. Anyway, the learned District Judge upon hearing the appellants allowed the application staying the operation of the impugned order of status quo. In view of the above, my considered view is that if the impugned order of status quo remains stayed, it may lead to serious consequences to any of the parties if the property in question is sold out by any of the parties and/or if any party is dispossessed by any adversary party from the suit land. Taking into account of all the aspects of the matter, the order of status quo passed by the learned trial Judge appears to be more reasonable, convincing and justified to me.
 
27. Under the aforesaid circumstances, my considered view is that the learned District Judge has committed illegality in staying the operation of the order of status quo passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram. 

28. Having considered all the facts and circumstances of the case, I find merit in this Rule. 

29. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. 

30. In consequence thereof, the impugned Order No. 1 dated 30-8-2022 passed by the learned District Judge, Chattogram allowing the application for stay in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 398 of 2022 and thereby staying the order dated 20-6-2022 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Chattogram in Other Class Suit No. 1141 of 2021 is, hereby, set-aside. 

31. However, the parties of the suit are directed to maintain status quo in respect of position and possession of the suit land in question and they are also directed not to sell the suit property to anybody else until the suit is disposed of on merit. 

32. The learned trial Judge is directed to proceed with the suit and dispose of the same on merit in accordance with law. 

Communicate the judgment and order to the learned Judges of the concerned Courts below, at once. 

End.
